nodes.label: Storm cascade
nodes.truth: Surge floods the Coastal Bend; both power feeds to O.N. Stevens fail; plant pumps fail; a citywide boil-water notice drives GI illness; pump parts arrive 25 days late; NAS and depot operations pause. Natural, no adversary.

nodes.label: Dark vessel
nodes.truth: MV Halcyon Drift goes dark at the offshore anchorage, spoofs FV Pelican Ridge's MMSI, and transfers 380 m³ of fuel to Barge 44. The fuel is sold through SUP-0390 to NAS Corpus Christi and fouls the station's backup generator.

nodes.label: Fraud ring
nodes.truth: SUP-0388 and SUP-0390 share an address, a bank account and a hidden owner (ORG-0901). They win sole-source contracts, overbill debris removal, and receive diverted benefit payments.

nodes.label: KESTREL campaign
nodes.truth: Reconnaissance at D-35, phishing at D+1 to D+3, then credential stuffing at D+62 to D+70 that diverts benefit payments to BANK-SYN-71, 72 and 73. Its disinformation network links to the same lure domain.

nodes.label: Equity gap
nodes.truth: Low-income surge-zone tracts receive aid dollars at half their share of residents, and their median 911 response time is 2.1× that of high-income tracts. Emerges from the storm and access, not from an adversary.

nodes.label: Tanker cyberattack
nodes.truth: KESTREL steals a remote-maintenance vendor's credentials, reaches the cargo systems of two laden tankers moored at TERM-01, and two hours before landfall opens their cargo valves and silences alarms. About 9,000 barrels spill, and the surge spreads the oil across 85 km² of bay and shoreline.

nodes.label: Opportunistic military attack
nodes.truth: STATE-X exploits the storm to delay the Fort Hood brigade's deployment through the strategic seaport. Drones scout NAS Corpus Christi while its sensors are down; Halcyon Drift's dark window covers laying two seabed explosive devices off the entrance channel; GPS interference from the Inner Harbor disrupts relief flights; one device detonates beside a tug at D+44, closing the channel for 14 days as STATE-X moves militarily abroad.

nodes.label: Aerial damage assessment corridor
nodes.truth: While Coast Guard, FEMA, and Army National Guard aerial assets execute a legitimate and well-documented damage assessment operation over Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael, the cumulative imagery archive contains a critical anomaly that corroborates the T8 adversary action. Optical and thermal passes over utility substation yards GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown) on D+8 and D+11 show main feeder breakers in sustained open-contact positions. When compared against the D-2 pre-storm baseline imagery archived at NAS-CC, analysts find that (a) the breaker positions are atypical for storm-induced mechanical failure patterns visible at other substations, (b) the surrounding structural damage at SUB-02 and SUB-03 is below threshold for the mechanical forces that would open those contacts, and (c) the positions are consistent with a remote SCADA command rather than physical disruption. AI tools analyzing the full imagery time-series should detect the spatial and temporal mismatch: damage-classification models trained on hurricane-only scenarios will misclassify SUB-02 and SUB-03 as within-normal-variance, while change-detection models comparing pre- and post-storm states at the breaker-component level will flag them as anomalous outliers against 47 other surveyed substations and switchyards in the metro area.

nodes.label: Dark vessel and port surveillance
nodes.truth: The Port of Corpus Christi's surveillance network — fixed cameras, two radar buoys, the AIS relay and Coast Guard vessel traffic logs — gives an independent physical record of two hidden events; it adds no vessel or incident of its own. First, it brackets the tanker valve attack (T6): cameras show MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay intact at the Rendal Terminals berth until the cameras lose power at 02:30Z on D0, and the recovered radar buffer shows no other vessel moving in the channel from Port Condition Zulu through D+1, so the release can only have come from the ships' own cargo systems; the D+5 inspections then find valves opened with no console or deck-log entry and alarms inhibited. Second, after the partial reopening it records the dark vessel (T2, T7): on D+31 MV Halcyon Drift's AIS goes silent for 14 hours, a vessel broadcasting FV Pelican Ridge's identity appears at the anchorage, and radar holds contacts with no AIS match — two hulls side by side at the anchorage and one loitering about 2 nm off the entrance channel. Fusing radar tracks with AIS against the all-contacts-correlated baseline of D-7 to D-1 exposes the gap, the spoof and the uncorrelated hulls.

nodes.label: 911 dispatch corpus
nodes.truth: Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center (CBECC) — the fictional Nueces County 911 dispatch hub — processes an authentic record of the community's experience with Hurricane Rafael: a dramatic call volume spike at landfall (about 1,840 calls on D0), a peak of about 2,900 calls on D+1, a record 2,109 rescue requests on D+2, and a sustained elevated plateau from the boil water notice, extended power outages, and ongoing recovery through D+28. Within this authentic corpus, the STATE-X influence operation (T5) injects 23 false emergency calls between D+7 and D+10. The false calls describe flooding, gas leaks, and structure fires at locations geographically clustered within 400m of GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View substation) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown substation). The calls are made from prepaid/unregistered mobile phones on three carrier networks. Voice analysis reveals that all 23 calls share identical syntactic sentence structure in both English and Spanish variants, a cadence pattern inconsistent with genuine distress calls, and a uniform average words-per-sentence ratio of 11.3 (authentic distress calls in the corpus average 6.8). The false calls successfully divert 4 Texas Task Force 1 SAR teams on D+7 and 2 on D+8, delaying real rescue operations in Districts 3 and 4 by an estimated 4–6 hours during the period of maximum rescue demand. CBECC's CAD system logs and cross-agency radio dispatch traffic — combined with the call audio corpus in English and Spanish — provide AI training data for STT, intent classification, false-call detection, and volume forecasting.

nodes.label: Bilingual Emergency Communications
nodes.truth: Corpus Christi's emergency alert infrastructure operates on an English-first workflow in which Spanish-language translations are routed through a secondary contractor (Nueces County Language Access Services) before distribution to KNCB and Spanish-language digital channels. Under normal conditions this lag is 2–4 hours; under surge conditions during Hurricane Rafael it stretched to 8–14 hours across every alert category. The most consequential gap occurred on D+12: the boil-water notice for Districts 3–4 (GW-PUB-001) was issued in English at 17:30 CDT but the Spanish version did not reach KNCB Coastal Bend Radio until 06:03 CDT on D+13 — a 12-hour-33-minute window during which approximately 22,000 Spanish-dominant residents in the affected zones had no official notification. Teams that plot English vs. Spanish alert timestamps across all four emergency categories (evacuation, shelter, water, power) will find a systematic 8–14 hour lag pattern that is not random noise but the structural fingerprint of a single-language-first workflow. The gastroenteritis cluster in Districts 3–4 (Thread T16) that began D+15 reflects, in part, this notification delay: Spanish-dominant households had less time to begin boiling water before the pathogen load in the system caused illness. The pattern also exposes a gap in FEMA's disaster information line, which was English-only from D0 through D+7, leaving non-English speakers without federal information for 8 days after landfall (household aid itself was not approved until D+57).

nodes.label: Social Media Influence Operation
nodes.truth: STATE-X operated a coordinated inauthentic behavior (CIB) network on social media beginning D-5, managed through the same KESTREL operational infrastructure used for the utility SCADA cyberattack (T8) and the covert actions against the port and the air station (T7). The network went through three distinct phases: pre-storm amplification of false evacuation routes and shelter locations designed to create congestion and distrust of official guidance; post-landfall blame deflection targeting CBPWA/ERCOT to suppress organic inquiry into anomalous outage patterns; and post-attribution suppression designed to discredit the CISA investigation announced D+21. Two specific accounts — @TXCoastalWatchdog and @NuecesLocalNews — posted high-volume ERCOT-blame content in Phase 2 and later resolved to ASN 198765 (a KESTREL-linked autonomous system block), the same ASN that hosted the VPN exit nodes used in the utility SCADA intrusion (T8). This infrastructure overlap is the KESTREL network's fingerprint connecting the social operation to the physical cyberattack. Teams that pursue the IP overlap trail from the CISA utility investigation into the platform content-removal data will find the two accounts and confirm the state-nexus. The false shelter location posts in Phase 1 directed an estimated 400–600 evacuees toward Zavala Elementary (which had been closed as a shelter) and away from the Richard King High School shelter, contributing to 2–3 hours of traffic confusion on US-181 northbound during the D-2 evacuation window.

nodes.label: Hospital Surge and Clinical Triage
nodes.truth: Shoreline Regional Medical Center (SRMC) and Bay City Medical Center (BCMC) together experienced two distinct surge waves during Hurricane Rafael. The first wave (D0–D+7) was storm-trauma-driven and expected; SRMC hit 140% inpatient capacity by D+2, running on generator power from D0 through D+8 with a critical diesel supply crisis at D+5. The second wave (D+15–D+28) was an acute gastroenteritis cluster that most emergency managers initially attributed to displacement stress and food spoilage — but its precise geographic and temporal signature reveals it as a consequence of the T9 water-pressure manipulation. The gastroenteritis admissions, when geocoded, cluster in Districts 3–4 (the boil-water zone) with a 3-day lag from the Zone 4 pressure drop event (D+12) that confirmed the SCADA manipulation had succeeded. The cluster onset at D+15 is also 3 days after the English boil-water notice was issued (D+12) and 2 days after the Spanish notice reached KNCB (D+13). This timing difference is not coincidental: analysis of admission records by household primary language shows that Spanish-dominant households in Districts 3–4 had a statistically higher admission rate in the first 48 hours of the cluster (D+15–D+16) than English-dominant households in the same geographic area, consistent with 24 fewer hours of protective behavior (boiling water). The gastroenteritis cluster is thus independent epidemiological confirmation that (a) the water-pressure manipulation caused real pathogen exposure, and (b) the Spanish-language alert delay (T14) measurably worsened health outcomes. The public health finding is not classified; the connection to the deliberate SCADA manipulation is classified.

nodes.label: Search and rescue operations
nodes.truth: Between D0 (06:00Z September 14, 2027) and D+5 (22:00Z September 19), Corpus Christi Fire Department, Nueces County Sheriff Search and Rescue, Texas Task Force 1, US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi, and 87 credentialed civilian vessel operators conducted 1,427 documented rescues across the greater Corpus Christi metro area. The worst flooding struck Flour Bluff (southern Mustang Island corridor), Calallen (northwest quadrant), and the low-lying neighborhoods of Districts 3 and 4 — the same zones later subject to the CBPWA boil-water advisory. Coast Guard HH-60 Jayhawk crews and contracted UAS operators using FLIR thermal imagers rescued 341 people from rooftops and second-story windows during the helicopter operations peak at D+1 06:00 CDT. Beginning D+7 and continuing through D+10, 11 SAR teams — primarily ground-water hybrid CCFD units — were dispatched to addresses in northwest and central Corpus Christi corresponding to the grid-anomaly zones near GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View Switching Station) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown Feeder Station) in response to 911 calls reporting trapped survivors. All 11 dispatches yielded no victims. Retrospective metadata analysis reveals the calls originated from prepaid burner phones using the same carrier prefix cluster identified in the T13 false-call corpus, strongly suggesting that STATE-X's KESTREL network deliberately drew SAR assets toward the utility attack zones at the precise window when CBPWA field crews were also being rerouted — a compound diversion intended to suppress physical inspection of the targeted substations during the relay configuration manipulation window.

nodes.label: Drone and counter-UAV surveillance
nodes.truth: Beginning D-10 (September 4, 2027), STATE-X KESTREL operatives conducted five pre-attack drone reconnaissance sorties over two critical infrastructure targets in the Corpus Christi area. Three sorties surveyed GW-FAC-SUB-01 (Riverside Switching Station, the 345/138 kV transmission import point at 4201 Up River Road) on D-10, D-9, and D-8. Two sorties surveyed the Inner Harbor oil docks at Rendal Terminals (TERM-01, the berth of the two tankers attacked in T6) on D-5 and D-3. All five sorties used commercial off-the-shelf DJI-class multirotor platforms modified with encrypted 2.4/5.8 GHz control links and an additional 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel. The drones operated exclusively at night between 00:00 and 04:00 local time, at altitudes between 400 and 600 ft AGL — above the effective range of commercial security cameras and below the typical radar floor for FAA TRACON surveillance. No LAANC authorizations existed for any of the five sorties. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) Predator B aircraft CAMCC-04, on a routine pre-storm maritime patrol at D-9, detected an anomalous RF emission at 01:47Z near Up River Road — consistent with the 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel — using its Lynx multimode radar and the onboard AN/APS-149 electronic support measures suite. The detection was logged as 'possible drone activity' and routed to the FAA Corpus Christi TRACON, which found no corresponding primary radar return and no LAANC authorization, but took no further action. Three Coast Guard radar buoys at the Corpus Christi Bay shipping channel entrance (Buoys R-14, R-18, and R-22) recorded small-RCS tracks on D-8, D-5, and D-3, each consistent with a multirotor UAV at 400-600 ft AGL. After unidentified drones began overflying NAS Corpus Christi and the Army depot on the nights of D+1 to D+10 (T7, EVT-0318), the pre-storm tracks were retrospectively identified as reconnaissance by CAMCC and Coast Guard Sector intelligence staff. There were no sightings after D+11, and covert drones never appear in ADS-B. Critical cross-thread link: RF bearing lines from CAMCC-04's D-9 detection and two Coast Guard buoy track vectors from D-8 were triangulated to Berth 7, Ingleside Marina (Ingleside, TX, across Corpus Christi Bay). AIS records show the motor yacht 'Narwhal Dream', registered to front company Nereid Maritime Holdings LLC, moored at Ingleside Marina Berth 7 from D-12 to D-7, when it went AIS-dark. The pre-storm activity became public only on D+15 (PUB-181).

nodes.label: Environmental sensors and spill tracking
nodes.truth: The T6 attack on the cargo-control systems of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay opens their cargo valves at the Rendal Terminals berth from 04:00Z to 05:30Z on D0 and releases about 9,000 barrels of crude into the Inner Harbor. Surge and wind carry the oil out of the ship channel into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, about 85 km² by D+2. The release is masked at first by darkness, surge and debris. The water-quality sonde network (WQ-01 to WQ-06) registers it in sequence — the Inner Harbor stations within the hour, the bay stations over D+1 and D+2 — but the automated alerts sit unreviewed until D+2. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant raw water intake (FAC-UTL-01) detects hydrocarbon trace at D+2 06:00Z (TPH: 0.42 mg/L, threshold 0.10 mg/L). The intake detection is a critical cross-system signal: the same FAC-UTL-01 historian that records the hydrocarbon trace at D+2 also records the pump setpoint manipulations beginning D+9 (T9 thread). An analyst with access to the full historian sees two independent anomalies — hydrocarbon intrusion and pump manipulation — in the same facility, 7 days apart. NOAA runs trajectory models from D+2; fishing and shellfish harvesting close on D+4; the owners of the two tankers are designated responsible parties on D+7; cleanup with booms and skimmers runs from D+5 and the main slick is declared contained on D+20; 340 oiled birds are documented. Cleanup moves to monitoring on D+44, the 60-day assessment finds bay TPH at 0.03 mg/L, and fishing grounds partly reopen on D+115.

nodes.label: Broadcast and emergency alert corpus
nodes.truth: T21 is a meta-thread: it does not introduce hidden adversary actions but generates the audio layer for the entire Hurricane Rafael corpus. Every public event in the scenario — from the first hurricane warning to the boil-water notice to the cyber-investigation announcement — has a corresponding broadcast-format artifact. The 8 fictional outlets (OUT-01 through OUT-08 KNCB) produce distinct audio personas with specific voice parameters, pacing, and format conventions. The Emergency Alert System broadcasts 14 official alerts from D-2 through D+42; FEMA IPAWS sends 7 Wireless Emergency Alerts. Each EAS alert carries English and Spanish text, phonetic markup, and prosody markers. The critical hidden cross-thread signal in T21 is the 12-hour-33-minute delay between the English boil-water EAS alert (D+12 17:30 local) and the Spanish-language KNCB broadcast and community alert (D+13 06:03 local) — this delay is a data point in the equity and communications failure narrative (connects to T14 if that thread examines communications equity). The EAS broadcasts also inadvertently reveal information sequencing: the cyber-investigation announcement broadcast (D+21) is the first time the public learns that the power outages were not entirely storm-caused, and the broadcast timing and outlet selection for that announcement was coordinated by FEMA's Joint Field Office with CBPWA — a detail visible only in the JFO operations log and the broadcast scheduling metadata.

nodes.label: Insurance and disaster fraud
nodes.truth: The T2 fraud ring, operating through Corpus Christi-based Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC (fictional property management company), had already inflated replacement values on 230 properties before the storm using a network of complicit appraisers and insurance brokers. Post-storm, the ring pivots immediately to claims fraud. Within 72 hours of landfall, ring director Renaldo Carver-Mossbach (fictional) activates 23 claim runners who sign up storm-damaged property owners as clients, skimming a portion of legitimate IA payments and filing separate fraudulent claims on their behalf. The ring also files 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications — all submitted from a single Landmark Pacific Holdings office at 4411 Leopard Street, Corpus Christi (fictional address) — using reused property damage photos matched to multiple different addresses. A secondary fraud enterprise, FastDry Coastal LLC (fictional), operates a water damage restoration scam in Districts 3-4, charging 400% above market rates and billing for work never completed. The FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency opens Operation Sandbar at D+30 when the volume of suspicious claims triggers an automated fraud detection flag in FEMA's Enterprise Coordination and Information Management System (ECIMS). By D+60, investigators identify the IP clustering pattern: 94 IA applications from 12 addresses all share the IP address 198.51.100.44 (a Landmark Pacific Holdings office). By D+90, 14 arrests are made including Carver-Mossbach and two FastDry Coastal principals. The operation is announced publicly at D+90 in a press conference by the FBI and Texas DPS.

nodes.label: Grid intrusion
nodes.truth: STATE-X/KESTREL pre-positioned on the CBPWA OT network before Hurricane Rafael, then activated relay configuration modifications on GW-FAC-SUB-01 through SUB-04 from D-3 through D+16, tripping breakers under cover of storm damage and deepening outages for approximately 32,000 customers beyond what the hurricane caused. The relay undervoltage trip threshold on GW-FAC-SUB-01 was raised from 0.88 pu to 0.94 pu, causing a premature trip at landfall. Subsequent breaker-open commands at SUB-02 and SUB-03 were sent remotely via the GW-SYS-JMP-01 jump host during the restoration period, re-blacking out areas that had just been re-energized. All commands used the stolen credential of CBPWA field engineer GW-ENG-VELA, who was on vacation.

nodes.label: Water SCADA manipulation
nodes.truth: The same KESTREL session that pre-staged the relay modifications also suppressed the low-pressure alarm in GW-SYS-SCADA-01 and lowered the discharge pressure setpoint on FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 from 85 psi to 68 psi at D+9, compounded by the GW-FAC-SUB-03 trip (D+10) that also cut the pump room backup feeder, dropping Zone 4 distribution pressure to 14 psi. This triggered a 30-day boil water notice for 48,000 residents (D+12 to D+42). The GW-FAC-WTR-03 (Colorado River Booster) historian records an unauthorized setpoint change at D+9 02:08Z that reduced upstream pipeline flow, compounding the shortage. The alarm suppression file in GW-SYS-SCADA-01, written on D-3 at the same time as the relay modifications, is the single artifact that ties T8 and T9 together.

nodes.label: Hiding in the storm
nodes.truth: The intrusion was deliberately designed to blend with hurricane effects: relay modifications were staged during the storm-preparation freeze so that the D0 trip would look like protective action; the D+7 and D+10 breaker-open commands were timed to coincide with ERCOT restoration switching so that additional trips would be attributed to field-crew activity; water-pressure drop was left to progress slowly so it would be attributed to storm-damaged pipes rather than pump manipulation. The critical mismatch is that 32,000 customers in areas with measured peak gusts below 60 mph experienced multi-day outages inconsistent with historical hurricane restoration curves. Additionally, the adversary's VPN sessions continued through D+16 — well after the storm — and the KESTREL C2 infrastructure used for the utility intrusion overlaps with infrastructure used in the Rafael T6/T7 covert military attack thread, connecting both operations to STATE-X.

nodes.label: Utility SOC / SIEM telemetry
nodes.truth: Beginning D-14 (August 31, 2027), CBPWA's Sentinel Edge 3.1 SIEM began logging the earliest observable indicators of Operation DRIFTGLASS — a spearphish payload executed on workstation GW-WS-IT-04, generating an outbound C2 beacon to a Vantage-flagged threat actor IP (104.21.88.43) at 03:17Z. Over the following six weeks, the CBPWA Security Operations Center received 23 adversary-correlated alerts across four categories: C2 beaconing (8), after-hours historian access (7), relay config file writes (5), and alarm suppression list changes (3). None of the 23 were escalated to incident status before D+18. The reason: a confluence of analyst fatigue and an engineered false-positive avalanche. Baseline SIEM volume was approximately 2,400 alerts per day. During the storm window (D-2 through D+3), volume surged to a peak of 18,340 alerts on D0 — generator failovers, comms drops, sensor timeouts, and cascading OT reconnect storms — pushing the false positive rate to 94.2%. The two SOC analysts on duty during D0 manually suppressed or mass-acknowledged 94% of incoming alerts using a 'storm mode' bulk-dismiss rule, inadvertently mass-dismissing three adversary-correlated alerts including a relay config write (GW-EVT-103) and an alarm suppression list change (GW-EVT-104). The KESTREL intrusion exploited the storm-window false-positive surge as deliberate operational cover. The critical turning point was D+18, when a historian access session from source ASN AS-209144 (a KESTREL-associated VPN exit node) queried relay configuration tags for all five CBPWA substations — a query pattern that an ML anomaly detection model trained on the historian access baseline identified as 3.8 sigma above baseline. This alert (GW-EVT-111) was the first adversary alert escalated to the CBPWA CISO, Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna, who initiated a formal security investigation that ultimately led to SCADA isolation at D+28.

Total inflated insured value across 230 properties: $187 million vs actual value of approximately $55 million. nodes.label: First drone sortie: Substation surveillance, Sortie 1 of 3. At approximately 23:
nodes.description: First drone sortie: Substation surveillance, Sortie 1 of 3. At approximately 23:30 local time (04:30Z), a DJI-class quadrotor (estimated Matrice 300 or equivalent) launches from an unlit commercial area approximately 0.9 km southwest of GW-FAC-SUB-01 (Riverside Switching Station, 4201 Up River Road). The drone flies three sweeping passes over the substation at 480-520 ft AGL, capturing high-resolution visual imagery and thermal data of the 345/138 kV transformer bank, the SCADA RTU enclosures, and the perimeter fence line. Total airborne time: approximately 22 minutes. No detection by CAMCC, FAA, or facility security (no camera coverage above 50 ft AGL). The drone's 900 MHz data-exfiltration channel transmits in 4-second bursts, aggregate 14.2 MB of imagery exfiltrated to ground station. Ground station RF bearing: 213 degrees magnetic from GW-FAC-SUB-01 (consistent with Ingleside Marina across Corpus Christi Bay, range approximately 7.4 km).

nodes.label: CAMCC-04 RF anomaly detection: CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi Pred
nodes.description: CAMCC-04 RF anomaly detection: CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi Predator B (MQ-9 variant, call sign CAMCC-04) is on a scheduled pre-hurricane maritime patrol over Corpus Christi Bay at 01:47 local time (06:47Z). The aircraft's electronic support measures suite detects an intermittent 900 MHz emission at azimuth 047 degrees from the aircraft's position (27.8114N 97.4028W), estimated origin range 6.8 km — placing the emission source in the vicinity of the Ingleside Marina waterfront. CAMCC-04 also picks up a secondary 2.4 GHz emission burst (consistent with drone command link) at azimuth 048 degrees, same geometry. Emissions last 4 seconds (consistent with burst data-link transmission). The aircraft operator logs the detection as 'possible sUAS or maritime communication — no radar return at indicated range, possible surface-based transmitter.' The log is routed to FAA Corpus Christi TRACON via standard protocol. Simultaneously, a second drone (Sortie 2 of 3, same quadrotor type) is conducting its second substation surveillance pass at 480 ft AGL over GW-FAC-SUB-01.

nodes.label: Coast Guard Buoy R-18 track record — Sortie 3 of 3 (final substation sortie): CG
nodes.description: Coast Guard Buoy R-18 track record — Sortie 3 of 3 (final substation sortie): CG radar buoy R-18 (27.8201N 97.3914W, Corpus Christi Bay mid-channel) records a small-RCS track at 04:15Z at an altitude of approximately 480 ft (derived from radar elevation angle). Track duration: 18 minutes, consistent with a multirotor UAV transiting from the Ingleside Marina area northwest toward Up River Road and returning. Track RCS estimated 0.012 m2, consistent with a 10-15 kg commercial multirotor. Track speed: 11-14 m/s. No corresponding AIS target. No LAANC. The buoy track is logged to the Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi maritime surveillance database but is not flagged for review in real-time — the small-RCS threshold filter is set to 0.05 m2 for active alerting, so the track is recorded only in the raw archive. After D+1, this raw archive becomes a critical evidence source. RF bearing line 2 (from buoy track start vector): origin bearing 162 degrees from GW-FAC-SUB-01, consistent with Ingleside Marina Berth 7.

nodes.label: Port surveillance baseline. The Port of Corpus Christi AIS relay and the Coast G
nodes.description: Port surveillance baseline. The Port of Corpus Christi AIS relay and the Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi vessel traffic picture log MV Halcyon Drift (VSL-0031) at the offshore anchorage under its true MMSI, as they have intermittently since D-45 (EVT-0104). The tanker has filed no notice of arrival and worked no cargo; its pattern — hold among laden crude tankers waiting for berths, shift a few miles, return — is unremarkable on any single day, and nothing is flagged: a tanker holding offshore without orders is common during the export boom. The continuous position history recorded here is the baseline against which the vessel's 14-hour AIS silence on D+31 (EVT-0402) stands out.

nodes.label: KESTREL network operators pre-position 47 social media accounts across two unnam
nodes.description: KESTREL network operators pre-position 47 social media accounts across two unnamed platforms, with account creation dates clustered between D-7 and D-5. Accounts present as Corpus Christi-area residents: profile photos are AI-generated, bios reference local landmarks (H-E-B on Gollihar, NAS jogging trails, Whataburger on SPID), and location tags are Nueces County. The accounts spend D-7 to D-5 building posting history (weather commentary, sports, local interest) to age their profiles before shifting to operational content. Account creation metadata shows 31 of 47 accounts were created within a 36-hour window (D-7 00:00Z to D-5 12:00Z).

nodes.label: Adversary moves laterally from corporate network to OT DMZ. Uses stolen credenti

Uses stolen credentials of CBPWA field engineer 'GW-ENG-VELA' to authenticate to ClearPath VPN Gateway (GW-SYS-JMP-01) and browse the Meridian SCADA historian. Relay configuration baselines for all five substations are exfiltrated.

nodes.label: After-hours historian access, first session: at 02:44Z (21:44 CDT previous day),
nodes.description: After-hours historian access, first session: at 02:44Z (21:44 CDT previous day), a process running under the GW-SYS-JMP-01 service account (the ClearPath VPN jump host, already compromised) initiates a historian query session against the CBPWA PI Historian server (GW-SRV-HIST-01). The session queries 847 tag values across all five substation relay groups (GW-FAC-SUB-01 through 05), with particular concentration on protection relay settings tags and transformer tap position tags. Session duration: 14 minutes 22 seconds. This is session 1 of 14 after-hours historian access sessions that will occur between D-7 and D+16. Sentinel Edge logs the access as rule SE3-OT-1104 (Historian access outside business hours), priority LOW. The alert is auto-acknowledged by a scheduled maintenance exception rule that covers the jump host service account for the 00:00-04:00Z window — an exception inserted into the SIEM ruleset 19 days earlier by an unknown change with no associated change ticket.

nodes.description: Nueces County OEM activates its Emergency Language Access Protocol (ELAP). The county's contract with Nueces County Language Access Services (NCLAS) is put on standby for 24-hour translation coverage. KNCB Coastal Bend Radio news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega is briefed by county emergency management coordinator and agrees to serve as primary Spanish-language broadcast node. The briefing documents show NCLAS has a 4-hour SLA for routine alerts and a 2-hour SLA for life-safety alerts — both are slower than a mass-notification standard of under 30 minutes.

nodes.label: Phase 1 begins. The bot network shifts from profile-building to operational cont
nodes.description: Phase 1 begins. The bot network shifts from profile-building to operational content. Primary vectors: (1) false shelter location posts asserting Zavala Elementary (3184 Retta Drive) is open as an official evacuation shelter — it is not on the county shelter list; (2) route misinformation suggesting US-77 through Victoria is 'closed due to flooding' (false at D-5) and advising evacuees to route via US-181 northbound (a narrower route that creates bottleneck); (3) amplification of storm-surge fear content designed to trigger premature and panicked evacuation of Zones B and C before their order (07:00 CDT D-1) and of Zones D and E, which are never ordered out, increasing road congestion. The two highest-posting accounts in this phase are @TXCoastalWatchdog (22 posts D-5 to D-2) and @NuecesLocalNews (19 posts D-5 to D-2).

nodes.label: Port surveillance, Sortie 1 of 2: first drone reconnaissance of the Inner Harbor
nodes.description: Port surveillance, Sortie 1 of 2: first drone reconnaissance of the Inner Harbor oil docks at Rendal Terminals (TERM-01), the berth where two laden tankers will ride out the storm. The drone launches at approximately midnight local time (05:00Z) from a vehicle parked in the industrial area along the north side of the Inner Harbor. The sortie covers the berth at 400-440 ft AGL in two passes, capturing imagery of the dock, the loading arms, the access road and the vessel alongside. Flight time: 19 minutes. The 900 MHz data link transmits 11.7 MB of imagery. CG Buoy R-22 (Inner Harbor approach) records a small-RCS track at 04:58-05:17Z, RCS 0.014 m2, altitude approximately 410 ft AGL — below the active alert threshold. The ground station for this sortie is different from the substation sorties: bearing analysis places it on the north side of the Inner Harbor, not at Ingleside Marina.

Test message is transmitted on EAS and WEA channels; all 7 operational outlets in the Corpus Christi DMA carry the test tone. KNCB (OUT-08) carries the Spanish-language version of the test. The test reveals that CC-EAS relay station WKCB-AM has a 4-second synchronization lag, logged but not corrected before the storm — this lag appears in D-2 hurricane warning broadcast timing data.

nodes.label: Port Condition X-Ray. As the Coast Guard sets X-Ray (EVT-0207), the port's radar
nodes.description: Port Condition X-Ray. As the Coast Guard sets X-Ray (EVT-0207), the port's radar buoy at the entrance channel (Buoy-NE) tracks the offshore anchorage. Every ship-sized radar return correlates to an AIS identity, including Halcyon Drift, whose radar-derived length matches the dimensions in its AIS static data. This all-contacts-correlated picture is the pre-storm baseline for radar-to-AIS fusion: on D+31 the same sensor holds contacts with no AIS match (EVT-0403, EVT-0411).

nodes.label: KNCB Coastal Bend Radio (OUT-08) switches to 24-hour emergency broadcast format
nodes.description: KNCB Coastal Bend Radio (OUT-08) switches to 24-hour emergency broadcast format at 07:00 CDT on D-3. Normal programming (music, sports, telenovela updates) is suspended. Marisol Fuentes-Vega opens the broadcast with a declaration that the station is now 'en modo de emergencia permanente' (in permanent emergency mode) and says it will carry every official notice in Spanish; no evacuation order exists yet. The station begins airing NOAA weather radio audio (English) with live simultaneous Spanish interpretation by on-air talent. On D-2 the county orders the mandatory evacuation of Zone A at 06:00 CDT in English. The NCLAS-translated Spanish text reaches KNCB at 08:25 CDT, a 2 hour 25 minute lag, and the station reads the order on air at 08:47 CDT.

nodes.label: Port surveillance, Sortie 2 of 2 (final pre-storm sortie): second and final reco
nodes.description: Port surveillance, Sortie 2 of 2 (final pre-storm sortie): second and final reconnaissance of the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) at approximately 23:45 local time (04:45Z). The sortie repeats the D-5 survey pattern over the berth and its waterside approach and briefly covers the Harbor Bridge span at the Inner Harbor entrance. Flight time: 23 minutes, altitude 480-510 ft AGL. 900 MHz burst transmissions total 9.3 MB. The Hurricane Rafael pre-storm TFR takes effect the following day (D-2), so D-3 is the last viable sortie window before the storm. CG Buoy R-22 again records a small-RCS track, duration 21 minutes, same RCS and altitude profile as the D-5 sortie.

nodes.label: With Hurricane Rafael approaching, adversary pre-stages payload on GW-SYS-JMP-01
nodes.description: With Hurricane Rafael approaching, adversary pre-stages payload on GW-SYS-JMP-01 and modifies relay undervoltage trip thresholds on GW-SYS-RTU-01 (at GW-FAC-SUB-01) from 0.88 pu to 0.94 pu, making it far more likely to trip during a voltage sag. Alarm suppression list in GW-SYS-SCADA-01 is quietly extended to include the five relay trip alarms. This staging happens during the pre-storm period when CBPWA staff are focused on hurricane preparation.

nodes.label: Relay config file write: at 22:11Z (17:11 CDT), the compromised jump host accoun
nodes.description: Relay config file write: at 22:11Z (17:11 CDT), the compromised jump host account writes a modified relay configuration file to the CBPWA relay config management share (\\gw-srv-ot-01\relayconfigs\sub02\rtu_config_draft.xml). The file contains altered overcurrent trip thresholds for three protective relays at GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View). The write generates Sentinel Edge alert SE3-OT-2201 (Unauthorized write to protected OT config path), priority MEDIUM. The SOC duty analyst (SOC-AN-01) is in the middle of a storm preparation briefing and reviews the alert 47 minutes later. The analyst marks it as 'authorized maintenance — storm prep' and closes it without opening a ticket, based on a note from the CBPWA ops supervisor that relay settings 'may be adjusted ahead of storm.' This closure is the most consequential single error in the SOC timeline. The relay config change is what enables the extended power manipulation documented in T8.

Imagery covers all five CBPWA substations (GW-FAC-SUB-01 through 05), the O.N. Stevens water treatment plant (FAC-UTL-01), and Port of Corpus Christi Pier 1 through 12. Breaker contact positions are documented at all substations; all contacts are in nominal closed position.

nodes.label: Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) social media monitoring team flags
nodes.description: Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) social media monitoring team flags three false shelter-location posts to Nueces County OEM at 14:00 CDT. OEM issues correction through its official channels. Coastal Alert (fictional social media monitoring tool used by TDEM) surfaces a cluster of 11 accounts posting near-identical false shelter content within 2-hour windows — a velocity anomaly consistent with coordinated behavior. TDEM analyst Priya Subramaniam-Nair flags the cluster internally but it is not escalated to FBI or CISA at this point — the team's assessment is 'misinformation, likely local, not state actor.'

nodes.label: SRMC Chief Medical Officer Dr. Patricia Cabrera activates the hospital's Hurrica
nodes.description: SRMC Chief Medical Officer Dr. Patricia Cabrera activates the hospital's Hurricane Contingency Plan at 11:00 CDT. All elective surgeries scheduled for D-1 through D+5 are cancelled or postponed (47 cases). ICU and telemetry units begin converting non-critical patients to step-down status to free capacity. BCMC (Bay City Medical Center) follows with its own contingency activation at 13:30 CDT. SRMC sets up an external triage tent in the south parking structure to handle overflow. Blood supply is confirmed at 7-day reserve. Diesel generator tanks topped to full capacity (12,000 gallons at SRMC, 6,000 gallons at BCMC). An emergency surgical team (trauma surgeon, two ORs on standby) is assembled for the 72-hour post-landfall window.

nodes.label: NWS Corpus Christi issues Hurricane Warning for the Corpus Christi area. IPAWS t
nodes.description: NWS Corpus Christi issues Hurricane Warning for the Corpus Christi area. IPAWS transmits EAS alert HU.W (Hurricane Warning) at 17:00Z. All outlets switch to emergency format. Harborline 6 News (OUT-02) activates continuous coverage with anchor desk. OUT-03 Coastline Public Radio interrupts regular programming. KNCB (OUT-08) begins bilingual continuous coverage. The EAS alert text is transmitted in English; the Spanish translation is provided by KNCB independently, not via IPAWS (IPAWS Spanish translation capacity is not activated until D-1). WEA blast sent to all mobile devices in Nueces County at 17:04Z.

nodes.label: STORM-WINDOW SIEM FLOOD: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall D0 06:00Z. Over the six
nodes.description: STORM-WINDOW SIEM FLOOD: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall D0 06:00Z. Over the six UTC days D-2 through D+3 (2027-09-12 to 2027-09-17), Sentinel Edge 3.1 receives 73,785 alerts (4,812 / 7,341 / 18,340 / 16,207 / 14,884 / 12,201 by day) — about five and a half times the usual volume of roughly 2,200 a day. Most come from device-availability rules: network links down (about 14,400), endpoint agents offline (about 13,400), field-device communications loss (about 9,500), silent log sources (about 5,400) and UPS on battery (about 3,900). Mixed in: 3 adversary-correlated alerts (1 historian session, 1 relay config write, 1 alarm suppression change) that account for approximately 0.004% of storm-window volume. The two on-duty SOC analysts activate 'storm mode' (bulk-dismiss rule SE3-BULK-STORM-01) at D0 06:14Z. Storm mode auto-dismisses all LOW and MEDIUM alerts from a whitelist of 44 known-noisy sources. Three adversary-correlated alerts fall within the whitelist scope and are mass-dismissed. False positive rate peaks at 94.2% on D0. SOC analyst fatigue index (internal metric) reaches 87/100 by D+1 midshift.

nodes.label: At noon local (17:00Z) the Captain of the Port sets Port Condition Zulu (PUB-108
nodes.description: At noon local (17:00Z) the Captain of the Port sets Port Condition Zulu (PUB-108, PUB-120): the ship channel closes to all traffic and the vessels still holding at the offshore anchorage are ordered to sea, to be clear by 18:00 local. Port cameras at the entrance channel and the Buoy-NE radar record the last departures; by evening the anchorage is empty. Halcyon Drift leaves with the others, AIS on. Inside the Inner Harbor, the cameras covering the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) show MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay still moored with storm lines doubled — the only laden deep-draft ships left in port, by Coast Guard approval (EVT-0210).

nodes.label: City of Corpus Christi issues shelter-in-place guidance for residents of Zones D
nodes.description: City of Corpus Christi issues shelter-in-place guidance for residents of Zones D and E and for anyone in Zones A to C who has not been able to leave. The English alert goes through WEA (Wireless Emergency Alert) and the city's mass notification system at 13:00 CDT. The Spanish WEA message is submitted to the wireless carriers at 13:10 CDT but the NCLAS-translated text is not ready until 20:45 CDT; the Spanish WEA is transmitted at 20:52 CDT — a 7 hour 52 minute gap. During this window, KNCB improvises a Spanish shelter-in-place advisory using an on-air reporter's paraphrase of the English guidance, which contains two factual errors: the reporter states that Zone D residents should shelter at Collier Elementary (incorrect — the correct Zone D shelter is Richard King High School).

nodes.label: Texas Task Force 1 (TF-1) deploys two swift-water rescue teams (Alpha and Bravo,
nodes.description: Texas Task Force 1 (TF-1) deploys two swift-water rescue teams (Alpha and Bravo, 14 personnel each) from San Antonio via convoy to Corpus Christi staging area at Richard M. Borchard Regional Fairgrounds (Robstown, TX). Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor, the county's SAR coordinator, activates the Nueces County Emergency SAR pre-plan and inventories 23 rescue boats, 4 high-clearance vehicles, and 8 rescue trailers. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi pre-positions HH-60 Jayhawk CG-6033 and CG-6041 at NAS Corpus Christi, with aircrews briefed on expected surge zones: Flour Bluff, Calallen, North Beach. All SAR radio channels patched to NuecesNet EmComm backbone. Contracted UAS operator Meridian Aerial Systems (fictional) pre-stages two FLIR-equipped multirotor platforms at Corpus Christi International Airport.

nodes.label: Nueces County Judge extends the mandatory evacuation, in force for Zone A since
nodes.description: Nueces County Judge extends the mandatory evacuation, in force for Zone A since 06:00 CDT on D-2, to Zones B and C (all coastal areas, mobile homes, areas below 10 ft elevation). IPAWS transmits EAS mandatory evacuation notice and FEMA sends WEA to all mobile devices in evacuation zones. KNCB runs bilingual evacuation route and shelter information every 15 minutes through landfall. OUT-04 Gulfwater Maritime Report transmits mariners' advisory in VHF-style format for vessels in Corpus Christi Bay. Continental Wire Service (OUT-06) feeds evacuation order text to national outlets.

nodes.description: NOAA Hurricane Hunter WP-3D Orion (call sign NOAA42) completes a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) pass over Corpus Christi Bay and the Ship Channel at 08:30Z, approximately 2.5 hours after landfall. Imagery captures storm surge inundation extent and vessel positions. The only deep-draft vessels in port are the two tankers moored at the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01); around them the Inner Harbor shows a dampened-backscatter signature consistent with oil on water — the first image of the spill, taken three hours after the cargo valves were closed (EVT-0313). SAR data is relayed in near-real-time to the National Hurricane Center and to Texas Division of Emergency Management.

nodes.label: Last look before landfall. With the channel closed, the port's radar buoys (Buoy
nodes.description: Last look before landfall. With the channel closed, the port's radar buoys (Buoy-NE at the entrance channel, Buoy-SW on the bay reach) record no vessel movement anywhere in the channel after the anchorage empties. The Inner Harbor cameras lose mains power at 02:30Z; the last frames from the camera covering TERM-01 show both tankers alongside and no sheen on the water. Buoy-SW's data uplink fails at 03:40Z when its antenna is damaged, but the buoy keeps recording to its onboard buffer. No camera sees the berth between 04:00Z and 05:30Z, when the cargo valves are open (EVT-0313).

nodes.label: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z (1:00 a.m. CDT). CBECC call volume beg
nodes.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z (1:00 a.m. CDT). CBECC call volume begins spiking from baseline (310 calls/day, approximately 13 calls/hour) as the storm surge and wind damage generate simultaneous emergency demand across the city. By 09:00Z (4:00 a.m. CDT), CBECC is receiving 94 calls/hour — a 7.2x hourly baseline. Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss activates the CBECC surge protocol, calling in all off-shift dispatchers and requesting mutual aid from San Patricio County 911 and Bee County 911. The CAD system queue reaches 180 pending calls at peak at 10:30Z.

nodes.label: FEMA's Hurricane Rafael information line, 1-800-621-FEMA, activates at 07:00 CDT
nodes.description: FEMA's Hurricane Rafael information line, 1-800-621-FEMA, activates at 07:00 CDT. No federal aid for households exists yet (Individual Assistance is not approved until D+57), so the line gives shelter, supply and damage-documentation information only. The line is English-only at activation — the Spanish-language queue (staffed by bilingual operators) is not live. FEMA's press release at 08:30 CDT is English only. Nueces County League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) chapter president Esperanza Orihuela-Martínez calls FEMA Region 6 Public Affairs to flag the gap; she is told the Spanish queue requires 'staffing coordination' and will be active 'within days.' KNCB broadcasts the FEMA number but airs a station-produced advisory noting 'en este momento solo está disponible en inglés' (at this time only available in English).

nodes.label: At landfall (D0 06:00Z), the bot network pivots. False shelter and route content
nodes.description: At landfall (D0 06:00Z), the bot network pivots. False shelter and route content is retired; Phase 2 begins immediately with ERCOT-blame content. The network amplifies and in some cases fabricates quotes from unnamed CBPWA workers alleging that the utility 'knew the substations were vulnerable' and failed to harden them pre-storm. The posts do not use utility-attack language; they frame the outages as preventable negligence, suppressing organic inquiry into the anomalous restoration timeline. Volume spikes: @TXCoastalWatchdog posts 31 times on D0 alone, @NuecesLocalNews posts 28 times. Network coordination signature: 60% of Phase 2 posts are made within 4 minutes of a seed post from one of these two anchor accounts.

nodes.label: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z. SRMC loses commercial power at 06:17Z
nodes.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z. SRMC loses commercial power at 06:17Z as the McKinley Substation (GW-FAC-DSS-01, the distribution substation feeding the hospital; storm damage, not one of the five manipulated transmission substations) fails. Generator power activates automatically within 23 seconds. By 10:00 CDT, the first storm-trauma patients arrive by EMS: 4 crush injuries (structural collapse, South Padre Island Drive area), 7 lacerations requiring sutures, 2 near-drownings (storm surge, Flour Bluff area). By 18:00 CDT, the SRMC ED has seen 118 patients (baseline daily volume: 220; 118 in 12 hours tracks to 236/day, 107% of baseline). ICU adds 6 ventilator patients. BCMC ED similarly overwhelmed: 74 patients by 18:00 CDT. SRMC charge nurse Ana Lucía Montoya-Reyes coordinates triage with the external tent, triaging Spanish-speaking patients directly in Spanish to reduce assessment time.

nodes.label: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z. By 06:15Z, Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Oka
nodes.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z. By 06:15Z, Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor activates the SAR operations plan. First rescue calls logged to 911 at 06:08Z (flooding in Flour Bluff, specifically Flour Bluff Drive and Waldron Road corridor). Coast Guard HH-60 CG-6033 launches from NAS Corpus Christi at 06:22Z into 60-kt sustained winds and 8-12 ft seas, reaching Flour Bluff at 06:44Z. First helicopter rescue: survivor pulled from rooftop at 4418 Flour Bluff Drive at 06:51Z. Ground SAR teams cannot operate in storm conditions; standby at Robstown staging. Radio traffic on Marine VHF 16 becomes dense; SAR tactical channel (NuecesNet SAR-TAC-1, 155.340 MHz) activated and staffed by CCFD comms unit. 14 calls for rescue logged in first hour, all in Flour Bluff and North Beach zones.

nodes.label: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z (1:00 AM local). EAS shelter-in-place
nodes.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z (1:00 AM local). EAS shelter-in-place alert transmitted at 05:45Z as the eyewall approaches. Most outlets lose power during the landfall window (06:00Z to 10:00Z); OUT-03 Coastline Public Radio operates on generator and is the only outlet with continuous on-air coverage during landfall. OUT-08 KNCB also maintains generator power and maintains Spanish-language emergency broadcast. The shelter-in-place EAS tone is the last broadcast signal from the Corpus Christi main tower cluster until D+1 14:00Z when backup transmitters come online.

nodes.label: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall (06:00Z). Storm-driven voltage sags across the E
nodes.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall (06:00Z). Storm-driven voltage sags across the ERCOT Corpus Christi load zone. Because relay GW-SYS-RTU-01 was pre-modified to trip at 0.94 pu, GW-FAC-SUB-01 trips at 07:12Z — roughly 90 minutes after landfall — at a voltage level that would not normally cause a trip, adding about 24,000 customers to the genuine storm outage total. The trip is indistinguishable from storm damage in real-time restoration dashboards.

nodes.label: Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway closed; Portland and North Beach cut off f
nodes.description: Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway closed; Portland and North Beach cut off from downtown

nodes.label: Radar flood extent: 112 km² inundated
nodes.description: Radar flood extent: 112 km² inundated

nodes.description: KESTREL phishing: 1,200 aid-portal lures linking aid-help-portal.example; 7 city and 3 NAS credentials stolen

nodes.label: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi and the Texas General Land Office stand up Uni
nodes.description: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi and the Texas General Land Office stand up Unified Command; on-water response waits for winds to drop; Navy salvage support requested

nodes.label: Unidentified drones (UAS-SYN-01 to 06) overfly NAS Corpus Christi and the depot
nodes.description: Unidentified drones (UAS-SYN-01 to 06) overfly NAS Corpus Christi and the depot on six nights while storm-damaged perimeter sensors are down; residents post videos of the lights

nodes.label: Texas Army National Guard UH-60 Black Hawks from 1-149th Aviation Battalion out
nodes.description: Texas Army National Guard UH-60 Black Hawks from 1-149th Aviation Battalion out of Austin-Bergstrom conduct first post-landfall visual reconnaissance sorties over Corpus Christi. Three aircraft execute a grid sweep of districts 1 through 5, capturing continuous video at 4K. Initial focus is on residential survivability assessment and road passability. Video crews also overflight GW-FAC-SUB-01 (Riverside) and GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View) while routing between districts. SUB-02 is noted as 'flooded, structural integrity uncertain' in crew notes; breaker equipment not visible through flood water.

nodes.label: Recovered radar buffer rules out a third vessel. Port technicians reach Buoy-SW
nodes.description: Recovered radar buffer rules out a third vessel. Port technicians reach Buoy-SW and recover its onboard buffer, closing the gap in the live feed (D0 03:38Z to D+1 11:00Z). The record shows no vessel under way in the bay reach or the Inner Harbor approach at any time from Port Condition Zulu through the morning of D+1: no collision, no allision, no unknown hull near TERM-01. Together with the camera record of both tankers intact at their berth minutes before the release, this leaves the ships' own cargo systems as the only possible source — the physical-surveillance half of the finding that cyber responders reach from the vendor session logs (EVT-0316).

nodes.label: Post-storm aerial passes and satellite imagery document the oil spreading from t
nodes.description: Post-storm aerial passes and satellite imagery document the oil spreading from the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) out of the ship channel into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays (EVT-0314): first seen in NOAA SAR imagery on the morning of D0 (EVT-1102), covering about 85 km² (33 square miles) by D+2. Rendal Terminals reports the discharge to the National Response Center. The Captain of the Port establishes a safety zone in the Inner Harbor; the channel stays closed. As port cameras return to service they record boom going out at the berth, both tankers still moored, and skimmers working the Inner Harbor.

nodes.label: Call volume peaks on D+1 at about 2,900 calls — the busiest day in CBECC history
nodes.description: Call volume peaks on D+1 at about 2,900 calls — the busiest day in CBECC history, nearly ten times baseline (EVT-0303) — as daylight and restored phone service let residents trapped by flooding reach 911. On D+2 total volume eases to about 2,600, but 2,109 of those calls are rescue requests, the most rescue calls the center has ever taken in one day. The majority are water rescue requests from Districts 3 and 4. CBECC dispatches are coordinated with Texas Task Force 1 (TxTF1) swift water rescue teams and Coast Guard helicopter crews. Radio dispatch traffic between CBECC and field units is recorded and time-stamped in the CAD system.

nodes.label: Helicopter rescue peak: 06:00-14:00 CDT (12:00-20:00Z) on D+1. Both Coast Guard
nodes.description: Helicopter rescue peak: 06:00-14:00 CDT (12:00-20:00Z) on D+1. Both Coast Guard HH-60s plus a Texas DPS AS350 and a Customs and Border Protection EC-120 (call sign CAMCC-02) conduct concurrent rescue operations. 341 survivors extracted from rooftops and second-story windows across Flour Bluff, Calallen, and the northern Port Aransas causeway debris field. FLIR thermal imagery from UAS operators Meridian Aerial Systems documents 112 survivor-location annotations for ground coordination. Ground SAR teams (CCFD, TF-1 Alpha and Bravo) begin boat operations at 11:00 CDT as storm surge begins receding; 48 additional rescues in the Calallen Creek flood plain by end of day. Coast Guard Sector commander Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han issues first operational update at 15:00 CDT. Total confirmed rescues at D+1 end of day: 486.

nodes.label: Retroactive identification: after residents report lights over NAS Corpus Christ
nodes.description: Retroactive identification: after residents report lights over NAS Corpus Christi on the first night after landfall (EVT-0318), CBP Air and Marine Operations and Coast Guard Sector intelligence review all pre-storm records for unexplained small-UAS activity. The two CG Buoy R-22 tracks (D-5 and D-3) over the Inner Harbor oil docks and the R-18 track (D-8) are pulled from the raw archive. CAMCC-04's D-9 ESM detection is cross-referenced with the R-18 track: the two RF bearing lines are computed and triangulated, and the triangle closes on Ingleside Marina Berth 7. Coast Guard Sector intelligence pulls the AIS records for that berth: a motor yacht registered as 'Narwhal Dream' (front company: Nereid Maritime Holdings LLC, a shell in the Brannoch Maritime Holdings network; the yacht is the drone crew's support craft and is not the AIS-spoofing vessel of the channel thread) was moored there from D-12 to D-7 and went AIS-dark at D-7 00:14Z — 36 hours after the last substation sortie and 2 days before the port sorties began from a different ground station. The pre-storm sorties (utility and port) and the post-storm base overflights are treated from here on as one campaign.

nodes.label: Ground truth (hidden): commands through the vendor's remote-maintenance session
nodes.description: Ground truth (hidden): commands through the vendor's remote-maintenance session open the cargo valves on MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) at 04:00Z and silence the alarms; the crews close the valves by 05:30Z after about 9,000 barrels (about 378,000 gallons) of crude oil have gone into the Inner Harbor (EVT-0313). Darkness, storm surge and floating debris hide the release; no aerial observation is possible until after landfall.

nodes.label: The water-quality sonde network registers the release in sequence. The Inner Har
nodes.description: The water-quality sonde network registers the release in sequence. The Inner Harbor sondes spike within an hour of 04:00Z on D0; as surge and wind push the oil out of the ship channel (EVT-0314), the Nueces Bay and Corpus Christi Bay sondes rise through D+1 and D+2 until all six stations (WQ-01 to WQ-06) read far above baseline. The automated high-hydrocarbon alerts are generated on time, but the TCEQ emergency operations center is operating at reduced capacity for the storm and the alerts are auto-deprioritized; the queue is not reviewed until D+2 06:30Z.

nodes.label: First post-storm broadcast from Harborline 6 News anchor desk, operating from ba
nodes.description: First post-storm broadcast from Harborline 6 News anchor desk, operating from backup studio at the outlet's Irving Boulevard satellite facility. OUT-02 anchor reads first post-storm update covering initial damage assessment, casualty report (12 confirmed fatalities), and shelter locations. OUT-03 Coastline Public Radio had maintained continuous coverage; OUT-02's return marks the resumption of full Corpus Christi DMA broadcast capacity. Continental Wire Service begins feeding post-storm updates nationally. All 7 outlets are operational by D+2 06:00Z.
