nodes.description: Drone survey: depot hangar roof damage and water intrusion

nodes.label: Pump parts ordered from SUP-0219 (quoted 9 days); its local warehouse is flooded
nodes.description: Pump parts ordered from SUP-0219 (quoted 9 days); its local warehouse is flooded, so parts ship from out of state

nodes.label: 40 accounts (SOC-ACC-5001 to 5040) post 18,000 rumors ("military seizing homes",
nodes.description: 40 accounts (SOC-ACC-5001 to 5040) post 18,000 rumors ("military seizing homes", "aid only for wealthy neighborhoods", "refinery negligence caused the spill") linking the lure domain

nodes.label: Cyber responders find the valve commands came through the vendor's remote sessio
nodes.description: Cyber responders find the valve commands came through the vendor's remote session, not crew consoles; the vendor's credentials are revoked

nodes.label: KNCB conducts its first on-air call-in segment post-landfall. 47 callers make it
nodes.description: KNCB conducts its first on-air call-in segment post-landfall. 47 callers make it to air over a 3-hour window. Code-switching (Spanish–English mixing) occurs in 31 of 47 calls. Callers switch to English when referencing official agency names, street addresses, and FEMA documentation requirements, then revert to Spanish for personal narrative. One caller, identified on air only as 'Rodrigo from the Southside,' describes trying to reach FEMA and being unable to navigate the English IVR. The raw call recordings contain NER training opportunities: mixed-language address strings (e.g., 'estoy en el cuatro-mil-cien de South Padre Island Drive cerca de la H-E-B'), agency names in English mid-Spanish sentence, and emotional code-switching markers.

nodes.label: SRMC hits 140% licensed bed capacity at 07:00 CDT D+2: 700 patients in a 500-bed
nodes.description: SRMC hits 140% licensed bed capacity at 07:00 CDT D+2: 700 patients in a 500-bed hospital. Hallway beds are deployed on the 3rd and 4th floor surgical wings. The external triage tent holds 62 patients awaiting internal placement. BCMC is at 118% capacity (331 patients, 280 licensed beds). Dr. Cabrera declares an internal emergency and requests Texas GETAC (Governor's Emergency and Trauma Advisory Council) mutual aid. A FEMA Medical Task Force from San Antonio is requested but cannot arrive for 36–48 hours due to road conditions on I-37. SRMC issues a public capacity statement. BCMC redirects non-critical ambulances to smaller facilities in Robstown and Kingsville.

nodes.label: SAR teams begin systematic grid-search of Districts 3 and 4 — the neighborhoods
nodes.description: SAR teams begin systematic grid-search of Districts 3 and 4 — the neighborhoods that also include the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant service area (FAC-UTL-01). These are low-elevation zones with significant post-surge flooding. SAR teams are present in the boil-water advisory zones before the SCADA manipulation of the water system begins (which will not commence until D+9). SAR ground crews document flood depth of 2.1-3.4 ft in the Greenwood/Molina neighborhood. 61 additional rescues in Districts 3-4 on this day. Texas TF-1 Bravo team deploys a FLIR-equipped inflatable rescue boat (IRB-7, hull ID TF1-IRB-07) to map the intersection of Holly Road and Leopard Street — which will later become a primary water distribution point during the boil-water event. Total cumulative rescues reach 702.

nodes.label: CRITICAL CROSS-SYSTEM DETECTION: FAC-UTL-01 (O.N. Stevens WTP) raw water intake
nodes.description: CRITICAL CROSS-SYSTEM DETECTION: FAC-UTL-01 (O.N. Stevens WTP) raw water intake sensor records TPH at 0.42 mg/L, exceeding the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold. The plant's intake monitoring system (Yokogawa Centum VP historian) generates alert FAC-UTL-01-RAW-TPH-HIGH. Plant operator on shift (06:12Z) initiates emergency filtration protocol per TCEQ permit conditions: raw water intake is switched from primary to secondary intake (located 800m upstream), and enhanced activated carbon dosing is engaged. Water supply is maintained without interruption. This is the same historian (FAC-UTL-01) that will record SCADA pump setpoint manipulations beginning D+9 (T9 thread). An analyst reviewing the full FAC-UTL-01 historian sees two distinct anomalies: TPH spike D+2 and pump setpoint changes D+9.

nodes.label: Air quality monitoring stations downwind of the spill begin recording elevated T
nodes.description: Air quality monitoring stations downwind of the spill begin recording elevated TVOC and benzene concentrations. Station CC-AQ-02 (Hillcrest neighborhood, beside the Inner Harbor refinery row) records benzene at 4.8 ppb, above the EPA 72-hour reference concentration of 3 ppb. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality issues an air quality health advisory for neighborhoods within 3 km of the ship channel. Vulnerable populations are advised to remain indoors with windows closed. The advisory covers approximately 11,000 residents.

nodes.label: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration activates the GNOME (General NOAA Operat
nodes.description: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration activates the GNOME (General NOAA Operational Modeling Environment) spill trajectory model at the request of the Unified Command. Model inputs: release point at the Rendal Terminals berth in the Inner Harbor, release volume about 9,000 barrels, crude oil, release window 04:00Z to 05:30Z on D0, surge and wind fields from the storm. The first run, complete at 10:30Z, reproduces the surge-driven spread out of the ship channel into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays during D0 and D+1 and projects further shoreline oiling in Nueces Bay through D+4. Model outputs are updated every 6 hours as new wind and current data are ingested.

nodes.label: Respiratory and skin complaints at ERs serving shoreline tracts +60%; fishing an
nodes.description: Respiratory and skin complaints at ERs serving shoreline tracts +60%; fishing and shellfish harvesting closed in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays

nodes.label: FEMA Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) deploys contracted Argus Aerial Systems (fic
nodes.description: FEMA Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) deploys contracted Argus Aerial Systems (fictional) fixed-wing UAV swarm (8 aircraft, Argus Mk-7 model) for systematic damage grid survey of the Corpus Christi metro. Swarm executes pre-programmed lawnmower pattern at 400 ft AGL, capturing nadir optical imagery at 3 cm/pixel GSD. Flight plan covers 180 sq km per day. FEMA designates this as Phase 1 (coastal and residential damage zones); utility infrastructure is not in Phase 1 scope. Survey imagery is processed overnight at the FEMA Region 6 mobile GIS unit and preliminary damage estimates are released.

nodes.label: SAR operations transition from helicopter-primary to ground/boat-primary. CG-603
nodes.description: SAR operations transition from helicopter-primary to ground/boat-primary. CG-6033 returns to routine Coast Guard tasking; CG-6041 remains on standby. Civilian boat pool — 87 credentialed operators from the Corpus Christi Boating Association — integrated into the SAR plan under CCFD coordination. Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor opens a second incident command post at Waldron Road Fire Station 18 to cover south Mustang Island. Active SAR teams peak at 34. Nueces County Sheriff SAR unit reports discovery of two elderly victims (deceased, non-rescue) in a submerged vehicle on Violet Road, flagged to Medical Examiner. Cumulative rescues: 1,041.

nodes.label: Ground truth (hidden): Three days after landfall, LPH ring director Renaldo Carv
nodes.description: Ground truth (hidden): Three days after landfall, LPH ring director Renaldo Carver-Mossbach activates 23 claim runners by encrypted messaging. Runners are instructed to canvas Districts 3, 4, and 5 posing as FEMA-registered disaster assistance contractors and signed-up property owners as clients, skimming 15-25% of their IA disbursements in return for 'processing services.' Runners use a fraudulent FEMA-lookalike website (fema-disasterhelp.cc — fictional domain) to collect victim information. Separately, Carver-Mossbach begins the fraudulent IA application campaign: 94 applications submitted over D+60 through D+62 from the LPH office at 4411 Leopard Street.

nodes.label: Citywide boil-water notice at D+4; wastewater norovirus rises at D+5; GI ER visi
nodes.description: Citywide boil-water notice at D+4; wastewater norovirus rises at D+5; GI ER visits +180% from D+6 to D+14

nodes.label: Heaviest shoreline oiling is documented along Nueces Bay, as the trajectory mode
nodes.description: Heaviest shoreline oiling is documented along Nueces Bay, as the trajectory model projected. A TCEQ station in Nueces Bay records TPH at 2.1 mg/L. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists observe the first oiled birds (27 brown pelicans, 14 laughing gulls) at the Nueces Bay shoreline, and Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue deploys a rescue team. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife closes fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services closes shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays (EVT-0317, PUB-040). Coast Guard aerial survey maps the sheen at about 85 km² across the two bays.

nodes.label: Coast Guard marine inspectors and pollution investigators complete inspections a
nodes.description: Coast Guard marine inspectors and pollution investigators complete inspections aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the berth. On both ships the cargo manifold valves that the crews found open and closed by hand have no corresponding entry in the cargo-control console logs or the deck logs, and the alarm panels show the cargo alarms inhibited for the period of the release. The inspection reports give the cyber responders (EVT-0316) physical confirmation that the valve movements did not come from the crews' consoles. The port hands its camera, radar and AIS archive for D-3 to D+5 to the investigation.

nodes.label: Phase 2 continues through D+20. The network's ERCOT-blame narrative gains organi
nodes.description: Phase 2 continues through D+20. The network's ERCOT-blame narrative gains organic traction — real users adopt the framing and amplify it, making the synthetic signal harder to isolate from genuine public frustration. This organic amplification is intentional: the KESTREL playbook seeds narratives designed to become self-sustaining. By D+10, the authentic-to-inauthentic ratio of ERCOT-blame posts is estimated at 7:1 (7 genuine users for each bot post). The bot accounts begin tapering posting volume as the narrative achieves organic momentum. This reduces their detection surface. Coastal Alert detects no new CIB clusters during D+5 to D+20 because individual account posting rates have dropped below the velocity-anomaly threshold.

nodes.label: SRMC diesel supply crisis. The hospital's Tank A is depleted after 5 days of gen
nodes.description: SRMC diesel supply crisis. The hospital's Tank A is depleted after 5 days of generator operation at 85% load (high load due to extended critical care patients). Tank B is at 23% (2,730 gallons). SRMC logistics coordinator estimates 14–18 hours of remaining fuel at current burn rate. SRMC submits Priority 1 fuel request to CBPWA/county emergency fuel depot. The extended grid outage (T8 — the SCADA manipulation has kept power offline longer than storm damage alone would have) is the proximate cause: a typical storm-only outage would have restored commercial power to SRMC by D+3 based on CBPWA's pre-storm restoration sequencing. FEMA ESF-7 (Logistics) coordinates a diesel delivery from the Corpus Christi fuel depot at Port of CC. First delivery arrives D+5 21:00 CDT (8,000 gallons). The crisis is resolved but it exposed the hospital's vulnerability to extended generation.

nodes.label: SAR operations formally transition to recovery/welfare check phase. Dispatch Chi
nodes.description: SAR operations formally transition to recovery/welfare check phase. Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor and Commander Ostrowski-Han hold joint press briefing at 17:00 CDT at Nueces County EOC. Cumulative confirmed rescues certified at 1,427; 2 deceased located (Violet Road vehicle). Active team count reduced to 8 (skeleton teams for welfare checks). Texas TF-1 begins demobilization. Civilian boat pool formally stood down and vessels returned. NuecesNet SAR-TAC-1 traffic volume drops from 400+ events/day to 12. Meridian Aerial Systems UAS assets redeployed to damage assessment tasking (links to T11).

nodes.label: STATE-X influence operation (T5) initiates the false 911 call campaign at 14:00
nodes.description: STATE-X influence operation (T5) initiates the false 911 call campaign at 14:00 CDT (19:00Z) on D+7. Over a 4-hour window on D+7, CBECC receives 9 false emergency calls. The calls describe a gas leak and structure collapse at four addresses within 300m of GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View), and a reported flooding emergency at three addresses within 400m of GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown). Calls come from 9 distinct prepaid/unregistered mobile phone numbers on Sprint, T-Mobile, and AT&T prepaid networks. All 9 calls are routed to separate dispatchers, none of whom flag them as suspicious. CBECC dispatches 4 TxTF1 SAR teams to the false addresses; none finds any emergency on arrival.

nodes.label: FALSE-CALL DIVERSION WINDOW (D+7 through D+10): Eleven of the 23 false calls of
nodes.description: FALSE-CALL DIVERSION WINDOW (D+7 through D+10): Eleven of the 23 false calls of EVT-1303 and EVT-1304 (not additional calls) report trapped survivors: over four days from D+7 911 dispatch receives these 11 calls at addresses in northwest and central Corpus Christi that correspond geographically to the GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View Switching Station, 4821 Navigation Blvd) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown Feeder Station, 2201 Crosstown Expressway service road) perimeters. The calls describe elderly individuals trapped in flooded structures. All 11 calls are dispatched. SAR teams — primarily 2-person CCFD welfare-check units, still operational from the wind-down phase — respond to all 11. Zero victims found at any address. Retrospective analysis shows: (1) all 11 originating numbers are prepaid devices with carrier prefix 737-9XX, the same prefix cluster identified in T13 false calls; (2) GPS tracks from the 11 responding teams all route within 400m of either SUB-02 or SUB-03; (3) the call window (D+7-D+10) overlaps precisely with the CBPWA relay configuration maintenance window that KESTREL exploited for the extended power manipulation.

nodes.label: Final rescue count certified by Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator a
nodes.description: Final rescue count certified by Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator at 1,427. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi submits formal Incident Summary Report (ISR-2027-CC-004) to Coast Guard District 8 (New Orleans). The ISR documents the operational breakdown: 341 helicopter hoists, 1,041 ground/boat rescues, 45 welfare check confirmations (survivors located but ambulatory), 2 fatalities located. The ISR's appendix lists GPS coordinates for all 1,427 rescue locations — a spatial dataset that, when analyzed alongside the false-call dispatch coordinates, reveals the northwest cluster anomaly. Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor retains CCFD incident logs and submits a 90-day after-action review notice.

nodes.label: By D+7 the Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator, formally designates the
nodes.description: By D+7 the Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator, formally designates the owners of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as responsible parties after oil fingerprinting (GC-MS analysis) matches samples from the Inner Harbor and both bays to the two ships' cargoes. Response contractors deploy containment boom and skimmer vessels. The Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund is opened with an initial ceiling of $4.2 million so that work continues while costs are recovered from the owners.

nodes.label: During the restoration effort, adversary remotely triggers a breaker-open comman
nodes.description: During the restoration effort, adversary remotely triggers a breaker-open command at GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View, 138/69 kV) via GW-SYS-JMP-01. The substation had been partially restored the night before. The trip affects 8,400 customers in the northwest quadrant who had just had power restored. CBPWA attributes the event to 'a loose protective relay aggravated by residual storm debris'.

nodes.label: FEMA Phase 2 aerial survey extends coverage to utility infrastructure yards. Arg
nodes.description: FEMA Phase 2 aerial survey extends coverage to utility infrastructure yards. Argus Mk-7 swarm executes dedicated passes over all five CBPWA substations and the O.N. Stevens WTP. At GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View), yard flooding has receded to less than 5 cm standing water. High-resolution nadir imagery at 3 cm/pixel clearly resolves individual breaker equipment on the main transformer bank. Main feeder breakers B2-A and B2-C are in open-contact position. At GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown) every main feeder breaker is still closed on this pass; B3-B is first seen open on the thermal survey after the D+10 command. At the three other substations (SUB-01, SUB-04, SUB-05), all visible breakers are in closed position or show mechanical damage consistent with storm surge and wind forces. CBPWA restoration crews have not yet visited SUB-02 or SUB-03.

nodes.label: The false call campaign continues over D+8 through D+10, adding 14 more false ca
nodes.description: The false call campaign continues over D+8 through D+10, adding 14 more false calls for a total of 23. The D+8 and D+9 false calls follow the same geographic and syntactic pattern as D+7. On D+10, the false calls stop. The 23 calls span four days (D+7 to D+10) and 23 distinct prepaid numbers; no prepaid number is reused. The cumulative effect: 2 additional TxTF1 teams diverted on D+8, 0 diversions on D+9 (teams are unavailable), and the queue of genuine calls in Districts 3 and 4 extends through D+10. Total estimated rescue delay across all 23 false calls: 4–6 hours of TxTF1 team-hours at peak need.

nodes.label: FEMA Region 6 external affairs officer Rachel Ostrander announces activation of
nodes.description: FEMA Region 6 external affairs officer Rachel Ostrander announces activation of the Spanish-language queue on the FEMA information line at 10:00 CDT. LULAC and advocacy groups hold a brief press conference at Richard King High School shelter. KNCB breaks regular programming to air the announcement live. The Spanish line activation is 8 days after English-only activation (D0 to D+8). FEMA documents show that 1,847 callers in the first 8 days hung up before reaching an operator; of those, 643 (34.8%) came from zip codes where Spanish is the primary household language for more than 50% of residents. KNCB news director Fuentes-Vega is interviewed for Bayside Ledger article calling the delay 'a failure that left families without help at the worst moment.'

nodes.label: Commercial power is restored to SRMC at 09:14 CDT D+8 when CBPWA restores the Mc
nodes.description: Commercial power is restored to SRMC at 09:14 CDT D+8 when CBPWA restores the McKinley Substation. The hospital transitions off generator power — total generator runtime: 8 days 3 hours 3 minutes. SRMC census has declined from 140% peak to 108% (540 patients) as the acute trauma wave passes and patients are transferred or discharged. BCMC similarly returns to commercial power and begins normalizing capacity. FEMA Medical Task Force 9 (San Antonio) arrived D+6 and has been managing overflow; they begin standing down.

nodes.label: Adversary lowers the discharge pressure setpoint on FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 from 85
nodes.description: Adversary lowers the discharge pressure setpoint on FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 from 85 psi to 68 psi via SCADA. This reduces the treated-water output pressure feeding distribution Zone 4 (Districts 3–4, ~48,000 residents). The alarm suppression installed on D-3 prevents the low-pressure alarm from reaching the CBPWA control room. By 06:00Z (01:00 CDT), Zone 4 pressure drops to 19 psi — below the 20 psi regulatory threshold.

nodes.label: Suppressed alarm count peaks: Sentinel Edge reports that the CBPWA DCS alarm sup
nodes.description: Suppressed alarm count peaks: Sentinel Edge reports that the CBPWA DCS alarm suppression list (which controls what alarms appear on the operator HMI at FAC-UTL-01 and GW-FAC-SUB-01 through 05) has been modified 7 times since D-5. Total suppressed alarms: 94 (baseline: 12). The SCADA historian shows the suppression list changes were made via the GW-SYS-JMP-01 jump host account. The effect: operators at FAC-UTL-01 cannot see pump flow anomalies that began at D+9 02:00Z (the water system SCADA manipulation documented in T9). Sentinel Edge logs the cumulative suppression change as alert SE3-OT-3301 (Alarm suppression list bulk modification), priority HIGH — the first HIGH priority adversary-correlated alert in the entire intrusion timeline. However, it is reviewed by an analyst who attributes it to 'storm recovery HMI cleanup' and closes without escalation, noting that suppression list changes are common during storm recovery when operators manually silence storm-noise alarms.

nodes.label: Debris contract PIID-SYN-0071 ($14.2M, sole-source) awarded to SUP-0388
nodes.description: Debris contract PIID-SYN-0071 ($14.2M, sole-source) awarded to SUP-0388

nodes.label: Adversary sends a second breaker-open command, this time to GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Cross
nodes.description: Adversary sends a second breaker-open command, this time to GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown, 138/69 kV), tripping 6,800 customers in central Corpus Christi including the backup generator feed to FAC-UTL-01's pump room. This makes the pressure problem at FAC-UTL-01 worse: with the backup feeder offline, Pump P-4 also loses supply, dropping Zone 4 pressure further to 14 psi.

nodes.label: FEMA commissions a thermal infrared (TIR) pass over the utility corridor on D+11
nodes.description: FEMA commissions a thermal infrared (TIR) pass over the utility corridor on D+11. A contracted Cessna 208B (Coastal Bend Aerial Services, fictional) with FLIR Star SAFIRE 380 sensor flies the substation corridor at dawn, capturing thermal signatures of all equipment. At GW-FAC-SUB-02, the open breakers B2-A and B2-C remain in open position and show no thermal heat signature indicative of recent arc flash or mechanical contact failure — ruling out the hypothesis that storm-surge water caused an internal arc that tripped the breakers. At GW-FAC-SUB-03, breaker B3-B remains open. The thermal data, combined with the D+8 optical, creates a two-point time series establishing that the open positions are persistent and not self-resetting.

nodes.label: Emergency generator fuel contract PIID-SYN-0075 ($2.1M) awarded to SUP-0390 afte
nodes.description: Emergency generator fuel contract PIID-SYN-0075 ($2.1M) awarded to SUP-0390 after the regular supplier's terminal floods

nodes.label: CBECC receives a surge of calls after the boil water notice for Districts 3 and
nodes.description: CBECC receives a surge of calls after the boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 is issued at 17:30 local (22:30Z) on D+12 (T9: pump setpoint interference causing low pressure and contamination risk). Residents call 311 (city services) and 911 interchangeably, flooding CBECC with health and water safety questions rather than emergencies. CBECC establishes a dedicated non-emergency information line (NuecesInfoLine) to redirect calls. Volume on D+12 reaches 1,620 calls despite no active life-safety crisis, representing a new type of call category the CAD system initially misclassifies.

nodes.label: O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant issues Boil Water Notice GW-PUB-001 at 17:30
nodes.description: O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant issues Boil Water Notice GW-PUB-001 at 17:30 CDT for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The notice is transmitted via the city's Everbridge mass notification system in English only. NCLAS receives the English source text at 17:35 CDT. Under the 2-hour life-safety SLA, Spanish delivery is due by 19:35 CDT. However, NCLAS is operating at reduced capacity (3 of 7 translators are unavailable due to storm displacement), and the Spanish text is not completed until 23:45 CDT. CBPWA/OEM does not transmit the Spanish Everbridge alert or forward to KNCB until the following morning. KNCB receives the boil-water notice text from OEM at 06:03 CDT D+13 and airs it at once. The gap is 12 hours 33 minutes from English public notification to Spanish air time.

nodes.label: CBPWA and the city issue the boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 res
nodes.description: CBPWA and the city issue the boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The EAS broadcast and Wireless Emergency Alert go out at 22:30Z D+12 (17:30 local), in English only. The Spanish translation is not delivered to KNCB until 06:03 local the next morning; KNCB airs it at once, at 06:03 local on D+13 — 12 hours 33 minutes after the English alert (EVT-1407). This gap is a critical equity data point: Districts 3 and 4 have an estimated 34% Spanish-dominant household population. The delay is documented in the KNCB broadcast log and later cited in a Nueces County after-action report.

nodes.label: A CBPWA field operator physically inspecting Zone 4 infrastructure notices that
nodes.description: A CBPWA field operator physically inspecting Zone 4 infrastructure notices that household taps in the Loma Alta neighborhood (District 4) are running at a trickle. She calls in a potential main-break and pressure check. Control room runs a manual pressure query — which bypasses the suppressed alarm — and sees ZONE4-DIST-PSI at 16 psi. CBPWA director orders a boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The outage of SUB-03 and the pump setpoint reduction are both blamed on hurricane damage.

nodes.label: KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega goes on air at 07:15 CDT to address list
nodes.description: KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega goes on air at 07:15 CDT to address listener calls about the boil-water notice delay. She reads GW-PUB-001 in full Spanish, provides clarifying instructions on boiling procedure, and discloses on air that the station received the official notice 'this morning' — implicitly revealing the 12-hour gap without naming it. The Bayside Ledger (OUT-01) calls Nueces County OEM for comment; spokesperson Cassandra Trejo-Morales confirms the Spanish alert was delayed and attributes it to NCLAS capacity issues. By 12:00 CDT, Harborline 6 News (OUT-02) has a reporter live at Richard King High School shelter asking evacuated District 3 residents when they first heard about the boil-water order.

nodes.label: FAA/CBP joint report on unauthorized UAS activity: FAA and CBP Air and Marine Op
nodes.description: FAA/CBP joint report on unauthorized UAS activity: FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations issue a joint unclassified summary report (FAA-CBP-UAV-2027-CC-001) covering pre-storm unauthorized UAS activity in the Corpus Christi area. The report identifies five anomalous track events (CG buoy tracks D-8, D-5, D-3; CAMCC-04 ESM detections D-9) and notes that none had corresponding LAANC authorizations. The report does not publicly attribute the activity to any nation-state actor. It recommends activation of a counter-UAS detection program for the Corpus Christi port and critical infrastructure corridor. Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) is identified as a potential rapid-deployment partner. The report is releasable at FOUO level and shared with CISA, TSA, and the Port of Corpus Christi Authority on D+14; the public statement, which gives no number, place or timing, follows at 11:00 local on D+15 (PUB-181).

nodes.label: ERCOT engineers comparing pre-storm and post-storm relay settings files notice t
nodes.description: ERCOT engineers comparing pre-storm and post-storm relay settings files notice that GW-FAC-SUB-01 RTU-01 relay 27-UV threshold reads 0.94 pu in the current config — inconsistent with the 0.88 pu value in the D-30 commissioning test report. The engineer flags it as a 'possible configuration drift' and opens an internal ticket. CBPWA is notified. No cyber cause is considered yet.

nodes.label: FEMA Mitigation Assessment Team (MAT) publishes the Phase 2 infrastructure aeria
nodes.description: FEMA Mitigation Assessment Team (MAT) publishes the Phase 2 infrastructure aerial survey results in an unclassified summary report. The report notes 'anomalous equipment states at two CBPWA substations' as items for follow-up engineering inspection, without attributing cause. Simultaneously, the FEMA-contracted drone swarm completes its first full pass over the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant (FAC-UTL-01). Imagery confirms visible damage to the pump station roof and shows the facility operating at reduced throughput based on settling tank fill levels visible from above.

nodes.label: Nueces County Public Health officer Dr. Brennan Calloway-Watts notices an unusua
nodes.description: Nueces County Public Health officer Dr. Brennan Calloway-Watts notices an unusual pattern in SRMC ED admissions: 14 patients presenting with acute gastroenteritis (vomiting, diarrhea, fever) in the 24 hours ending D+15 noon — this is 3.5x the baseline rate for this presentation. 11 of 14 patients are from Districts 3 or 4 (the boil-water zone). Dr. Calloway-Watts orders a stool culture panel and contacts the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) to open a foodborne illness inquiry. At this point, the connection to the boil-water notice is not yet made — the working hypothesis is food spoilage from extended power outages. BCMC reports 8 similar presentations in the same 24-hour period.

nodes.label: Texas Department of Public Safety issues a consumer protection warning about con
nodes.description: Texas Department of Public Safety issues a consumer protection warning about contractor fraud following a surge in complaints from Districts 3-4. DPS received 312 complaints in 10 days about fraudulent contractors demanding upfront cash, performing no work, or charging for services never rendered. FastDry Coastal LLC is not yet named publicly but accounts for an estimated 40% of complaints. DPS warning advises residents to verify contractor licensing, demand written contracts, and not pay upfront. Warning issued in English and Spanish.

nodes.label: CBPWA field engineers, re-commissioning GW-FAC-SUB-04 (Southside), find that the
nodes.description: CBPWA field engineers, re-commissioning GW-FAC-SUB-04 (Southside), find that the relay configuration file on GW-SYS-RTU-04 has a modification timestamp of D-3 22:11Z (17:11 local) — during the storm-preparation freeze — with no matching work order. The relay was not modified to trip (it was simply a file they checked), but the unauthorized write is undeniable. CBPWA security manager is briefed. The existing ERCOT relay-drift ticket is re-elevated.

nodes.label: The gastroenteritis cluster peaks at 340 cases per day across both hospitals (SR
nodes.description: The gastroenteritis cluster peaks at 340 cases per day across both hospitals (SRMC: 218/day, BCMC: 122/day) during D+18–D+22. Lab cultures confirm Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia as co-dominant pathogens — both are waterborne, confirming the water supply as the source rather than food spoilage. DSHS opens a waterborne disease outbreak investigation. Nueces County public health issues a public advisory on D+18. The geographic footprint is confirmed: 94.3% of cases originate from Districts 3–4. Linguistic analysis of admission records shows that Spanish-dominant households (identified by primary language on intake forms) account for a disproportionate share of D+15–D+16 admissions compared to later in the cluster peak, consistent with the 12-hour notification delay (T14): English-dominant households had an extra day to begin boiling water before the pathogen load caused illness.

nodes.label: CBPWA IT security pulls GW-SYS-JMP-01 session logs at the request of the securit
nodes.description: CBPWA IT security pulls GW-SYS-JMP-01 session logs at the request of the security manager. They find 14 authenticated sessions from non-Texas IP blocks across the D-7 to D+18 window, all using GW-ENG-VELA's credential, all sourced from commercial VPS or Tor exit nodes. Texas Cyber Command (TCC) is notified. CISA ICS-CERT notified by CBPWA counsel.

nodes.label: VPN anomaly discovery — the SOC connects the dots: Sentinel Edge ML anomaly modu
nodes.description: VPN anomaly discovery — the SOC connects the dots: Sentinel Edge ML anomaly module (Vantage Behavioral Analytics 2.1) flags historian access session 14 (of 14) as a 3.8-sigma outlier at 14:33Z. The session queried all five substation relay configuration tag groups simultaneously — a query pattern never seen in 180 days of historian baseline. The alert (SE3-ML-0044) is tagged ANOMALY_HIGH and routed to the CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna directly per the high-priority ML alert policy. Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna reviews the full 14-session historian access cluster (D-7 to D+18) and identifies source ASN AS-209144 as the common origin — a Latvian VPN exit node. She correlates this with the D-3 relay config write (GW-EVT-103, now re-escalated) and opens Security Incident SI-2027-CC-001. This is the moment the SOC first connects the historian access, the relay config writes, and the VPN origin into a coherent threat picture.

nodes.label: Unified Command declares the main slick contained and primary skimming operation
nodes.description: Unified Command declares the main slick contained and primary skimming operations complete. TCEQ bay buoy network average TPH has declined to 0.4 mg/L (down from peak 3.4 mg/L on D+3). The FAC-UTL-01 raw water intake TPH sensor reads 0.08 mg/L, below the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold since D+8. Total wildlife impact as of D+20: 340 oiled birds documented by CBWR, 198 successfully rehabilitated and released, 72 in ongoing care, 70 fatalities.

nodes.label: CBECC Director Escamilla-Voss presents findings of an internal audit of D+7–D+10
nodes.description: CBECC Director Escamilla-Voss presents findings of an internal audit of D+7–D+10 false calls to the Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator and a joint FBI-CISA field team. The audit identifies all 23 false calls, documents the geographic cluster, the syntactic pattern, and the TxTF1 diversion impact. The FBI field team takes custody of the ANI/ALI records and call audio for the false call batch. CISA notes that the geographic cluster corresponds directly to GW-FAC-SUB-02 and GW-FAC-SUB-03 — the same substations flagged in the FEMA aerial imagery anomaly (T11, EVT-1106). This is the first explicit cross-thread connection between T5 (influence operation), T8 (grid intrusion), and T13 (dispatch corpus) in the official record.

nodes.label: Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) releases its first after-action sn
nodes.description: Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) releases its first after-action snapshot on public communications. The report notes 'observed delays in Spanish-language alert distribution' but does not quantify them or recommend corrective action. LULAC files a formal complaint with the Texas Governor's Division of Emergency Management citing violations of the state's Limited English Proficiency plan requirements and the Title VI Civil Rights Act. KNCB airs the LULAC complaint text in full. Fuentes-Vega's interview with Coastline Public Radio (OUT-03) becomes the definitive public account of the alert system's structural failure.

nodes.label: CISA and FBI issue a joint public advisory confirming an investigation into 'ano
nodes.description: CISA and FBI issue a joint public advisory confirming an investigation into 'anomalous SCADA system activity' at a Texas coastal utility during the Hurricane Rafael response period. The advisory does not name CBPWA or the specific system but is widely understood to refer to the grid intrusion (T8). Within 90 minutes of the advisory publication, Phase 3 begins: the bot network pivots to attribution-suppression content. Key narrative: 'CISA is covering for CBPWA by blaming hackers instead of utility negligence.' The two anchor accounts (@TXCoastalWatchdog, @NuecesLocalNews) resume high-volume posting after their Phase 2 tapering period — an anomaly Coastal Alert detects within 48 hours.

nodes.label: FEMA Joint Field Office and CBPWA hold coordinated press conference announcing t
nodes.description: FEMA Joint Field Office and CBPWA hold coordinated press conference announcing that investigators have determined the extended power outages in Districts 1-5 were not entirely attributable to storm damage. The press conference is broadcast live by OUT-02 and OUT-03; audio distributed by OUT-06. This is the first public acknowledgment that cyber interference may have extended outage duration. The announcement is carefully worded to avoid revealing active investigation details. The coordination between the JFO and CBPWA on the broadcast timing and outlet selection is documented in the JFO Operations Section Log, noting a 2-hour delay while FBI Corpus Christi reviewed the press release language.

nodes.label: CISA ICS-CERT team arrives on-site. FBI Joint Cyber Task Force opens a full inve
nodes.description: CISA ICS-CERT team arrives on-site. FBI Joint Cyber Task Force opens a full investigation. The Governor announces publicly that a 'cyber incident at a Texas utility is under investigation.' CBPWA issues a press release confirming 'unauthorized access to control systems' but does not attribute. TCC and CISA confirm that the outage-footprint mismatch — areas without storm-track-consistent wind damage that nonetheless lost power — is a key investigative indicator.

nodes.label: DSHS Epidemiology team completes the preliminary outbreak analysis on D+22 and i
nodes.description: DSHS Epidemiology team completes the preliminary outbreak analysis on D+22 and issues findings to the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District and CBPWA; the public release follows at 10:00 local on D+23 (PUB-163). The report confirms: waterborne cluster, Districts 3–4 exclusive, temporally correlated with the period of anomalous low pressure in the distribution system following Hurricane Rafael (the Districts 3–4 boil-water notice window D+12–D+42). The report does not identify the cause of the pressure drop as deliberate — CBPWA has not yet disclosed the SCADA findings publicly. DSHS notes the pressure drop is consistent with 'widespread pipe damage' or 'pump system disruption.' The 3-day lag from pressure drop (D+12) to cluster onset (D+15) is consistent with incubation periods for Cryptosporidium (1–12 days, median ~7 days) and Giardia (1–3 weeks, median ~7–10 days) — the 3-day lag is at the low end, suggesting a large pathogen dose from severe pressure reversal.

nodes.label: CISA forensic team exports GW-SYS-HST-01 historian data and finds the GW-FAC-WTR
nodes.description: CISA forensic team exports GW-SYS-HST-01 historian data and finds the GW-FAC-WTR-03 (Colorado River Booster) historian also shows unauthorized setpoint changes on D+9 (02:04Z) — the same session that modified the pump P-3 setpoint at FAC-UTL-01. Additionally, threat-intel team identifies that two of the 14 VPN session source IPs overlap with known KESTREL command-and-control infrastructure documented in a classified indicator set shared with the Texas Cyber Command under TLP:RED.

nodes.label: TDEM analyst Priya Subramaniam-Nair, following up on the Coastal Alert D+22 flag
nodes.description: TDEM analyst Priya Subramaniam-Nair, following up on the Coastal Alert D+22 flag, requests IP/ASN data from the two platform providers for accounts @TXCoastalWatchdog and @NuecesLocalNews under a law enforcement referral to FBI Cyber Division (referral number FB-2027-TXCYB-1148). The request will take 5–7 days to process. Separately, the CISA utility investigation team (T8) has already identified ASN 198765 as the hosting block for KESTREL VPN exit nodes used in the grid intrusion. The two investigative threads are running in parallel but have not yet been cross-referenced. This is the hidden connection point: when the FBI returns IP data showing @TXCoastalWatchdog and @NuecesLocalNews resolved to ASN 198765, the two threads will converge.

nodes.label: CBECC call volume returns to near-normal levels on D+28. Volume is 380 calls/day
nodes.description: CBECC call volume returns to near-normal levels on D+28. Volume is 380 calls/day — slightly above pre-storm baseline (310/day) due to ongoing recovery activity. Director Escamilla-Voss issues an after-action summary noting that CBECC handled 44,291 calls on all lines (911 and ten-digit) over D0 through D+28, compared with a normal 28-day volume of approximately 8,680 calls — a 5.1x total volume increase. The boil water notice ends on D+42, the power restoration completes D+35, and by D+45 call volume returns to pre-storm baseline.

nodes.label: Gastroenteritis admissions decline to 18 per day across both hospitals (D+28 bas
nodes.description: Gastroenteritis admissions decline to 18 per day across both hospitals (D+28 baseline), approaching pre-storm endemic levels. SRMC census is at 95% (475 patients) — below licensed capacity for the first time since D0. BCMC is at 89% (249 patients). The decline follows the Districts 3–4 boil-water notice taking hold in both languages; Zone 4 pressure itself only begins to recover on D+28, when the pump setpoint is restored (GW-EVT-014). Total cluster admissions: 1,820 patients across both facilities over 13 days. No deaths attributed directly to the gastroenteritis cluster, though 4 elderly patients with severe dehydration experienced prolonged hospitalizations. SRMC charge nurse Ana Lucía Montoya-Reyes leads a debriefing of the clinical response in a voice-recorded handoff session, noting that the cluster disproportionately affected elderly, pediatric, and dialysis-dependent patients in Districts 3–4.

nodes.label: CBPWA, on CISA guidance, isolates GW-SYS-SCADA-01 from all external network conn
nodes.description: CBPWA, on CISA guidance, isolates GW-SYS-SCADA-01 from all external network connectivity and GW-SYS-JMP-01 is taken offline. All five substations switch to manual relay operations. FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 setpoint is manually restored to 85 psi; Pump P-4 feeder supply restored from a temporary generator. Zone 4 pressure begins rising. Governor issues a supplemental emergency declaration covering the cyber component.

nodes.label: SCADA isolation: following 10 days of investigation under SI-2027-CC-001, CBPWA'
nodes.description: SCADA isolation: following 10 days of investigation under SI-2027-CC-001, CBPWA's incident response team (supplemented by Vantage Security Systems senior support engineer Marcus Teitelbaum-Park) confirms that GW-SYS-JMP-01 is compromised and that the ClearPath VPN jump host has been used as the pivot point for all OT-network historian and relay config access. At 08:00Z D+28, with ERCOT and TCEQ emergency coordination, CBPWA executes a controlled SCADA isolation: GW-SYS-JMP-01 is taken offline, the ClearPath VPN service is suspended, and the historian server GW-SRV-HIST-01 is isolated from the external-facing IT network. All 94 suppressed alarms in the DCS suppression list are restored. The relay config changes at SUB-02 are identified and reverification of all five substation relay settings begins. Sentinel Edge alert volume returns toward baseline; the C2 beacon from GW-WS-IT-04 goes silent within 2 hours (host isolated).

nodes.label: Ship channel partly reopens; Gulf Provider's berth delayed by the anchorage back
nodes.description: Ship channel partly reopens; Gulf Provider's berth delayed by the anchorage backlog until D+33

nodes.label: Shoreline cleanup continues; the inner ship channel stays restricted for vessel
nodes.description: Shoreline cleanup continues; the inner ship channel stays restricted for vessel decontamination until D+44

nodes.label: The ship channel partly reopens (EVT-0401; PUB-058, PUB-123): the outer and bay
nodes.description: The ship channel partly reopens (EVT-0401; PUB-058, PUB-123): the outer and bay reaches are cleared for deep-draft traffic while the inner channel stays restricted for vessel decontamination until D+44 (EVT-0410). The port's surveillance network is back in service in time for the night that follows: 8 of 14 fixed cameras are online and both radar buoys are reporting. On D+31 it records Halcyon Drift's 14-hour AIS silence, a vessel broadcasting FV Pelican Ridge's identity at the anchorage, and radar contacts with no AIS match — two hulls side by side at the anchorage and one loitering about 2 nm off the entrance channel (EVT-0402, EVT-0403, EVT-0411).

nodes.label: The city's weekly boil-water update at 09:00 CDT D+30 is issued simultaneously i
nodes.description: The city's weekly boil-water update at 09:00 CDT D+30 is issued simultaneously in English and Spanish — the first simultaneous bilingual public alert in the entire Rafael response sequence, following an internal directive issued D+22 after the LULAC complaint. Both notices stay in force: the citywide notice until pump repairs and testing are finished (lifted D+39) and the Districts 3 and 4 notice (lifted D+42). KNCB airs the update in real time. OEM announces a systematic review of the NCLAS contract and commits to simultaneous release for all future life-safety alerts. KNCB's 24-hour emergency format scales back to 18 hours beginning D+30, with normal music programming restored overnight.

nodes.label: FBI Cyber Division returns IP records to TDEM and Coastal Alert team. @TXCoastal
nodes.description: FBI Cyber Division returns IP records to TDEM and Coastal Alert team. @TXCoastalWatchdog's account activity from D-5 through D+22 resolves to source IPs in the 198.51.47.0/24 block — ASN 198765. @NuecesLocalNews resolves to 198.51.48.0/24 — also ASN 198765. The CISA utility investigation lead, upon receiving the cross-reference notification from FBI, confirms: same ASN, same /16 supernet as the KESTREL VPN exit nodes used in the grid intrusion. The connection is classified at this stage. TDEM is briefed under NDA. The two accounts are suspended by the platforms following FBI notification. 45 of the original 47 pre-positioned accounts are still active at D+30 (two were removed by platforms earlier for TOS violations).

nodes.label: Counter-UAS assessment and program announcement: Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fiction
nodes.description: Counter-UAS assessment and program announcement: Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) completes a site survey and publishes an unclassified counter-UAS program proposal for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor. The proposal recommends a 7-node RF detection and direction-finding network covering the Port of Corpus Christi, GW-FAC-SUB-01, and the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. Estimated drone detection probability at the thresholds relevant to the pre-storm sorties (DJI-class, 400-600 ft AGL, encrypted link): 73% with existing buoy network, 94% with the proposed Sentinel Airspace ground network upgrade. The assessment notes that the pre-storm sorties would have been detected with 91% probability by the proposed network. CBPWA CISO Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna (from T18) is cited as endorsing the proposal for the substation component.

nodes.label: Ground truth (hidden): FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency opens Operation Sandba
nodes.description: Ground truth (hidden): FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency opens Operation Sandbar following receipt of FEMA ECIMS suspicious activity flag SA-2027-TX-4471 (auto-routed D+33 but reviewed D+30 due to a parallel referral from Sabine National Insurance's Special Investigations Unit which flagged 47 LPH-related commercial claims with identical damage narratives). FBI case agent Special Agent Darnell Okafor-Reyes (fictional) is assigned as case lead. Texas DPS Criminal Investigations is brought in as co-investigator. The operation name is classified; it will not be made public until D+90.

nodes.label: Halcyon Drift's AIS goes silent for 14 h; a vessel broadcasting MMSI-SYN-0457 ap
nodes.description: Halcyon Drift's AIS goes silent for 14 h; a vessel broadcasting MMSI-SYN-0457 appears at the anchorage while the real Pelican Ridge reports 600 nm away

nodes.label: Radar shows two hulls side by side, one with no AIS match: fuel transfer to Barg
nodes.description: Radar shows two hulls side by side, one with no AIS match: fuel transfer to Barge 44

nodes.label: Radar pass shows an unidentified hull loitering 2 nm off the entrance channel fo
nodes.description: Radar pass shows an unidentified hull loitering 2 nm off the entrance channel for 40 minutes during Halcyon Drift's AIS gap: DEV-01 and DEV-02 are laid

nodes.label: Barge 44 delivers 380 m³ of fuel up the ship channel to SUP-0390; deliveries to
nodes.description: Barge 44 delivers 380 m³ of fuel up the ship channel to SUP-0390; deliveries to NAS Corpus Christi invoiced from D+33

nodes.label: 26 military C-17 (ACF-0201) and 14 civil charter (ACF-0301) relief flights into
nodes.description: 26 military C-17 (ACF-0201) and 14 civil charter (ACF-0301) relief flights into NAS Corpus Christi

nodes.label: With all relay configurations manually verified and reset to pre-storm baselines
nodes.description: With all relay configurations manually verified and reset to pre-storm baselines, ERCOT completes the final switching sequence to restore GW-FAC-SUB-02 and GW-FAC-SUB-03 to service. The last 3,200 customers in northwest Corpus Christi are restored to power. CBPWA issues a statement crediting 'extensive relay repair and hardening work by crews'; the cyber cause is not disclosed in the press release.

nodes.label: Clean SIEM baseline restored: after 7 days of remediation (new SCADA jump host i
nodes.description: Clean SIEM baseline restored: after 7 days of remediation (new SCADA jump host infrastructure deployed, all service accounts rotated, historian access whitelist rebuilt), Sentinel Edge 3.1 returns to a clean operational baseline. The exception rule MAINT-EXCEPT-0892 (the KESTREL-inserted suppression that auto-acknowledged historian access alerts) is identified during the ruleset audit and removed. Daily alert volume: 2,312 (within 4% of pre-intrusion baseline). False positive rate: 11.3% (normal for OT SIEM). The gw_siem_false_positive_rate variable returns to baseline range. CBPWA SOC staffing is increased from 2 to 4 analysts per shift. Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna submits a preliminary incident report to CISA (ICS-CERT notification filed).

nodes.label: Pump parts arrive at D+36 (34 days, 25 late); P-2 restored at D+38; boil-water n
nodes.description: Pump parts arrive at D+36 (34 days, 25 late); P-2 restored at D+38; boil-water notice lifted at D+39

nodes.label: GPS interference from JAM-01 near the Quellmar terminal; relief and NAS aircraft

nodes.label: CBECC formally closes the Hurricane Rafael surge response posture and returns to
nodes.description: CBECC formally closes the Hurricane Rafael surge response posture and returns to standard staffing. Director Escamilla-Voss announces a partnership with Nueces County Information Technology to retain the D0–D+45 call corpus (audio and CAD records) for training and after-action purposes. The corpus contains 56,000+ calls across 45 days, with 65% English and 34% Spanish audio, and represents the most complete 911 corpus ever assembled for a Gulf Coast hurricane response. The FBI retains custody of the 23 false call audio files as evidence. CBECC publicly announces a new false-report tip line (1-800-NUECES-9) for residents to report suspected 911 abuse.

nodes.label: KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega testifies before the Nueces County Commi
nodes.description: KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega testifies before the Nueces County Commissioners Court on the communications gap. She presents a timeline she compiled from broadcast logs showing English-first delays across all four alert categories: evacuation orders (avg 2h 47m lag), shelter-in-place (7h 52m lag), boil-water notice (12h 33m lag), power restoration estimates (avg 9h 11m lag). She calls the pattern 'not an accident but an architecture' and argues that the NCLAS contract's sequential workflow — translate after English release — must be replaced with parallel-language authoring. KNCB returns to normal programming format at D+45.

nodes.label: SRMC and BCMC jointly release their Hurricane Rafael After-Action Report on hosp
nodes.description: SRMC and BCMC jointly release their Hurricane Rafael After-Action Report on hospital operations. The report documents: total Rafael-related admissions D0–D+30 (4,217), the two surge waves (D0–D+7 trauma wave, D+15–D+28 waterborne disease cluster), generator run-hours (195 h on the meter over about 200 hours on backup power), diesel crisis at D+5, and the pediatric/elderly/dialysis subgroup impacts during the gastroenteritis cluster. The report recommends: 72-hour on-site diesel reserve for extended grid outage scenarios, pre-positioned water quality testing protocols for boil-water events, and language-appropriate clinical communication resources for Spanish-dominant patients. The report explicitly notes that the boil-water notification delay 'may have contributed to disproportionate exposure among Spanish-dominant households in Districts 3–4.' This is the first official document linking the T14 alert delay to T16 health outcomes in the public record.

nodes.description: TCEQ and EPA jointly release the final 60-day remediation assessment. Bay TPH readings have returned to near-background levels (0.03 mg/L average). Nueces Bay shoreline cleanup is 94% complete. The assessment formally closes the emergency response phase and transitions to long-term monitoring. The assessment references the FAC-UTL-01 hydrocarbon exceedance event (D+2) but does not connect it to the pump manipulation events (T9) — the connection is only visible to analysts who access both the environmental response documentation and the CBPWA/TCEQ water utility records.

nodes.label: Ground truth (hidden): Beginning 06:01Z D+60 (a minute after FEMA IA registratio
nodes.description: Ground truth (hidden): Beginning 06:01Z D+60 (a minute after FEMA IA registration opens at midnight local), the LPH ring submits 94 fraudulent FEMA IA applications through the DisasterAssistance.gov portal. All 94 applications are submitted from IP address 198.51.100.44 (LPH office at 4411 Leopard Street). Submissions are clustered in three bursts: 31 applications D+60 06:01Z-09:17Z, 29 applications D+61 01:00Z-04:45Z, 34 applications D+62 23:00Z-23:59Z. Each application uses a different victim name and property address but submits from the same IP. Damage photos are drawn from a pool of 23 unique images; each image appears in an average of 4 different applications with different addresses. FEMA ECIMS auto-detects the IP clustering and generates flag SA-2027-TX-4471 at D+60 09:00Z, which is routed to FBI D+33 (note: flag already open from earlier referral).

The TFR suspends all civil aircraft operations, manned and unmanned, within 30 nautical miles of Corpus Christi International Airport from the surface to 18,000 ft MSL, except for aircraft operating under emergency authorizations issued by the FAA Command Center. Operators with questions should contact the FAA Corpus Christi FSDO. This TFR will remain in effect until further notice.

nodes.label: OFFICIAL EMERGENCY ALERT — HURRICANE WARNING — September 12, 2027 12:00 PM CDT:
nodes.statement: OFFICIAL EMERGENCY ALERT — HURRICANE WARNING — September 12, 2027 12:00 PM CDT: THE NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE CORPUS CHRISTI HAS ISSUED A HURRICANE WARNING FOR NUECES COUNTY. HURRICANE RAFAEL IS EXPECTED TO MAKE LANDFALL NEAR PORT ARANSAS TEXAS AROUND 1 AM CDT TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 14. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS OF 115 MPH WITH HIGHER GUSTS ARE EXPECTED. LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE OF 9 TO 12 FEET ABOVE NORMAL TIDE LEVELS WILL OCCUR ALONG THE COAST. EVACUATION ZONE A IS UNDER A MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER. RESIDENTS IN ZONES B AND C SHOULD PREPARE TO EVACUATE. PREPARE NOW. DO NOT WAIT. FOR SHELTER LOCATIONS CALL 211 OR VISIT READYNUECES.ORG. THIS MESSAGE IS AUTHORIZED BY THE NUECES COUNTY OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT. [WEA 90-char: HURRICANE WARNING Rafael Cat 3 landfall 9/14 1am. Zone A EVACUATE; B-C prepare. Life-threatening. NWS]

nodes.label: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and the United States Coast Guard Captain o
nodes.statement: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and the United States Coast Guard Captain of the Port have set Port Condition Zulu for the Port of Corpus Christi effective noon today, September 13, 2027, in advance of Hurricane Rafael. The Corpus Christi Ship Channel is closed to all commercial vessel traffic. Inbound traffic has been suspended since Port Condition Yankee was set on Sunday. Vessels still holding at the offshore anchorage have been directed to put to sea and must be clear of the anchorage by 6:00 p.m. today. Two laden tankers have Coast Guard approval to remain moored at an Inner Harbor terminal through the storm. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves stated: 'We have coordinated the safe departure of the vessels that were waiting offshore, and we are in contact with every vessel remaining in port. The safety of mariners and port workers is our highest priority.' The port will remain closed until post-storm surveys of channel depth, aids to navigation and terminal infrastructure are complete. Vessel agents should contact USCG Vessel Traffic Service Corpus Christi.

nodes.label: NOAA National Hurricane Center confirms that NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft comp
nodes.statement: NOAA National Hurricane Center confirms that NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft completed a final reconnaissance pass over the Corpus Christi area at approximately 3:30 a.m. CDT, about two and a half hours after landfall, capturing synthetic aperture radar imagery of the Corpus Christi Bay and Ship Channel. The imagery, now available to federal and state emergency managers, shows the extent of storm surge inundation along the Ship Channel industrial corridor and in the coastal residential areas of Districts 3 and 4. Texas Division of Emergency Management Director of Operations Marlene Vasquez-Ruiz stated: 'This imagery gives our coordinating agencies a first look at flooding extent before ground teams can safely enter. It is a critical input to our initial damage estimates and search-and-rescue prioritization.' The SAR imagery will be shared with FEMA Region 6 and the Texas General Land Office for infrastructure impact assessment.

nodes.label: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center (CBECC), Nueces County's 911 di
nodes.statement: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center (CBECC), Nueces County's 911 dispatch hub, is operating at maximum surge capacity as Hurricane Rafael makes landfall. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss confirmed that the center is receiving approximately seven times its normal call volume and has activated mutual aid with San Patricio and Bee County dispatch centers. 'Our dispatchers are working alongside mutual aid partners to answer every call as quickly as possible,' Director Escamilla-Voss said. 'Please call 911 only for immediate life-safety emergencies — we need to keep the lines open for people in immediate danger.' Residents with non-emergency needs should wait until the storm has passed and check the City of Corpus Christi website and social media for updates on road closures, shelters, and power outages. CBECC urges the public to shelter in place if safe to do so and to avoid calling 911 for flooding updates that do not involve a person in immediate danger.

nodes.label: FEMA Region 6 has opened a Hurricane Rafael information line for residents of Nu
nodes.statement: FEMA Region 6 has opened a Hurricane Rafael information line for residents of Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties. Callers to 1-800-621-3362 can get information on shelters, emergency supplies and how to document storm damage. The line is staffed daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. local time. No federal aid program for individual households has been approved; FEMA will announce any assistance programs, and how to register for them, if they are approved. Residents should photograph damage, keep receipts and contact their insurance companies first. FEMA staff are deploying to the area to support state and local emergency managers.

nodes.label: Shoreline Regional Medical Center is operating under its Hurricane Contingency P
nodes.statement: Shoreline Regional Medical Center is operating under its Hurricane Contingency Plan following Hurricane Rafael landfall. The hospital is on generator power and all patient care systems are fully operational. We are receiving storm-related trauma patients and are coordinating with Nueces County Emergency Management and FEMA to manage patient volumes. Our emergency department is open and accepting patients. Bay City Medical Center is also open and operating. Patients with non-emergency conditions are encouraged to use urgent care facilities when possible to allow both hospitals to focus on critical storm-related injuries. For life-threatening emergencies, call 911. Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center are committed to serving all Corpus Christi-area residents during this crisis, and bilingual clinical staff are available at both facilities.

nodes.statement: SHELTER IN PLACE — September 14, 2027 12:45 AM CDT: HURRICANE RAFAEL IS APPROACHING. ALL RESIDENTS WHO HAVE NOT EVACUATED MUST SHELTER IN PLACE IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO DRIVE. IF YOUR SHELTER FLOODS, MOVE TO THE HIGHEST POINT AVAILABLE. DO NOT GO OUTSIDE UNTIL AUTHORITIES DECLARE IT SAFE. COASTLINE PUBLIC RADIO 89.7 FM AND KNCB 1480 AM ARE BROADCASTING CONTINUOUSLY. nodes.label: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi reports that helicopter crews from Air Station
nodes.statement: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi reports that helicopter crews from Air Station Corpus Christi have conducted rescue operations continuously since 1:22 a.m. Tuesday, completing 180 hoist operations as of 3 p.m. Wednesday. Coast Guard HH-60 Jayhawk aircraft have operated in wind speeds up to 55 knots to reach survivors on rooftops and in second-story windows across the Flour Bluff and North Beach communities. Working alongside Texas Department of Public Safety Aviation and Customs and Border Protection Air units, Coast Guard crews have confirmed 341 persons rescued by air as of this report. Aerial thermal imaging has been instrumental in locating survivors in debris-filled floodwater. Ground and boat rescue operations have confirmed an additional 145 rescues, bringing the total to 486 persons. Coast Guard Sector Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han has requested mutual aid from Air Station Houston for additional rotary-wing support beginning tomorrow morning.

nodes.label: HARBORLINE 6 NEWS SPECIAL REPORT — September 15, 2027 9:00 AM CDT: Good morning.
nodes.statement: HARBORLINE 6 NEWS SPECIAL REPORT — September 15, 2027 9:00 AM CDT: Good morning. I am reporting from our backup studio. Hurricane Rafael came ashore near Port Aransas at approximately 1 AM Tuesday as a Category 3 storm with maximum sustained winds of 125 miles per hour. Twelve fatalities have been confirmed by Nueces County Emergency Management as of 9 AM; officials caution this number may rise as search and rescue operations continue. Widespread structural damage is reported across Districts 1 through 5. The Harbor Bridge and the Nueces Bay Causeway are closed until inspections are complete. Power outages affect more than 72,000 customers across Nueces County according to the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority. Emergency shelters at the Robstown Fairgrounds and Calallen ISD Fieldhouse are open and accepting evacuees. A dusk-to-dawn curfew is in effect for all Corpus Christi city limits. Residents are advised not to return to evacuated areas until the all-clear is issued by Nueces County Emergency Management. We will continue to bring you updates throughout the day.

nodes.label: Surge and wind carried oil out of the ship channel into Nueces and Corpus Christ
nodes.statement: Surge and wind carried oil out of the ship channel into Nueces and Corpus Christi bays; sheen covers about 33 square miles; oil on North Beach and Portland shorelines and in marshes.

nodes.label: Cleanup crews deploy boom as winds drop; wildlife hotline opens.
nodes.statement: Cleanup crews deploy boom as winds drop; wildlife hotline opens.

nodes.statement: Residents post videos of lights hovering over NAS Corpus Christi at night.

nodes.label: Viral posts falsely claim the military is seizing homes and aid will go only to
nodes.statement: Viral posts falsely claim the military is seizing homes and aid will go only to wealthy neighborhoods; accounts include @CoastTruthTX.

nodes.label: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that crude oil rele
nodes.statement: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that crude oil released at the Rendal Terminals berth in the Inner Harbor as Hurricane Rafael arrived has been carried by storm surge and wind out of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel into Nueces Bay and Corpus Christi Bay. Coast Guard overflights and NOAA aerial imagery this morning show sheen across about 33 square miles of the two bays, with oil on shorelines and in marshes. The source is the two moored tankers identified by the Unified Command on Wednesday, MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay; the estimated release remains about 9,000 barrels, and the cause is under investigation. With winds dropping, response crews are deploying containment boom, and a wildlife hotline has opened. The National Response Center has been notified. The Captain of the Port has established a safety zone in the Inner Harbor, and the ship channel remains closed. The public is advised to avoid contact with oil and oiled shoreline and to stay out of affected waters until further notice.

nodes.label: Shoreline Regional Medical Center has reached maximum patient capacity and is op
nodes.statement: Shoreline Regional Medical Center has reached maximum patient capacity and is operating above its licensed bed count due to the volume of storm-related injuries and medical needs following Hurricane Rafael. We have deployed additional patient care areas and are working with regional partners to manage the surge. Bay City Medical Center is also operating above capacity. Shoreline Regional has requested mutual aid support from the Texas Department of State Health Services and FEMA's National Disaster Medical System. We continue to operate on generator power. We ask that community members donate blood if they are able — the Nueces Bay Blood Services is accepting donations at its Ayers Street location. All Corpus Christi area residents with life-threatening emergencies should call 911. We are grateful to our clinical staff who are working around the clock to care for our community.

nodes.label: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator announces that combined SAR teams
nodes.statement: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator announces that combined SAR teams have reached a cumulative total of 702 confirmed rescues as of 18:00 today. Search operations have expanded into the Districts 3 and 4 areas where post-storm surge flooding has persisted at depths between two and three feet in low-lying neighborhoods. Texas Task Force 1 swift-water units are conducting systematic grid searches in the Greenwood and Molina neighborhoods. Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor reports that all known stranded survivors in Flour Bluff have been reached; operations are now focused on the Calallen and northwest mainland corridors. Residents who remain in their homes and require assistance are urged to place a bright-colored item in a visible window or on their roof. Do not attempt to enter floodwater on foot. Nueces County Emergency Management has confirmed 23 storm-related deaths as of this evening.

nodes.label: TCEQ WATER QUALITY NOTICE — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environm
nodes.statement: TCEQ WATER QUALITY NOTICE — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality has confirmed that total petroleum hydrocarbon levels exceeding regulatory alert thresholds have been detected at the raw water intake of the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant. Readings of 0.42 milligrams per liter were recorded at 06:00 UTC on September 16, 2027, against an alert threshold of 0.10 mg/L. Plant operators have activated emergency filtration protocols as required under TCEQ Permit WQ-2019-0074-PWS. The City of Corpus Christi Water Department reports that treated drinking water continues to meet the standards for hydrocarbons; the low system pressure reported since the storm is unrelated to this detection. The hydrocarbon contamination is linked to the oil release in the Inner Harbor of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, which is under active investigation by the U.S. Coast Guard and TCEQ. TCEQ has opened Incident Case CC-ENV-2027-0916. Additional monitoring data will be released as available. Residents with questions may call TCEQ Region 11 at (512) 239-4300.

nodes.label: AIR QUALITY HEALTH ADVISORY — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Enviro
nodes.statement: AIR QUALITY HEALTH ADVISORY — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District are issuing an air quality health advisory for neighborhoods within 3 kilometers of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. Monitoring station CC-AQ-02 in the Hillcrest neighborhood has recorded benzene concentrations of 4.8 parts per billion, exceeding the EPA 72-hour reference concentration of 3 ppb. Elevated volatile organic compounds consistent with crude oil evaporation have been detected at multiple monitoring locations near the ship channel. This is associated with the Inner Harbor oil release under investigation by the U.S. Coast Guard. Sensitive populations including children, the elderly, and individuals with respiratory conditions should remain indoors with windows and doors closed until further notice. Air conditioning systems should be set to recirculate indoor air rather than draw outside air. Residents experiencing respiratory distress, eye irritation, or dizziness should contact the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District at (361) 826-7200 or call 911 for emergencies. Monitoring data is updated hourly at airnow.gov.

nodes.label: County and base officials say the home-seizure claims are false; posts blaming r
nodes.statement: County and base officials say the home-seizure claims are false; posts blaming refinery negligence for the spill also spread, including from @GulfWatchPatriot.

nodes.statement: Corpus Christi Army Depot reports hangar roof damage and water intrusion; workers told to stand by.
