nodes.statement: Harbor Bridge and Nueces Bay Causeway reopen after inspection.

nodes.label: Church and neighborhood hubs hand out food and water before official distributio
nodes.statement: Church and neighborhood hubs hand out food and water before official distribution reaches some neighborhoods.

nodes.label: ERs see respiratory and skin complaints from residents near oiled shorelines; he
nodes.statement: ERs see respiratory and skin complaints from residents near oiled shorelines; health officials advise avoiding contact with oil.

nodes.label: Ships that rode out the storm at sea return to the offshore anchorage to wait fo
nodes.statement: Ships that rode out the storm at sea return to the offshore anchorage to wait for the channel to reopen; the channel stays closed while it is surveyed and the spill is contained.

nodes.label: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator Lt. Col. Raymond Okafor-Williams
nodes.statement: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator Lt. Col. Raymond Okafor-Williams announced today that the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center handled about 2,900 emergency calls on Wednesday, September 15 — the busiest day in CBECC history and nearly ten times a normal day — and processed a record 2,109 rescue requests on Thursday, September 16, the most rescue calls the center has taken in a single day. The rescue surge was driven primarily by residents trapped by floodwater in Districts 3 and 4. 'Our dispatchers and the swift water rescue teams from Texas Task Force 1 worked through the night and into the next day to reach everyone who called,' said Okafor-Williams. 'We are proud of the professionalism shown by every member of the CBECC team.' On landfall day, Tuesday, September 14, the center took about 1,840 calls, about 1,100 of them rescue-related. Over the first three days of the storm response, CBECC handled more than 7,300 calls, compared to fewer than 1,000 calls during a normal three-day period. The center has sustained mutual aid staffing from San Patricio and Bee County, and anticipates call volume to remain elevated for several weeks as recovery operations continue.

nodes.label: DISASTER FRAUD WARNING — September 17, 2027: The Texas Office of the Attorney Ge
nodes.statement: DISASTER FRAUD WARNING — September 17, 2027: The Texas Office of the Attorney General and FEMA are warning Corpus Christi area residents about price gouging and contractor fraud following Hurricane Rafael. Reports are already emerging of contractors demanding large upfront cash payments and then failing to perform work. Texas law prohibits price gouging during a declared disaster. Warning signs of contractor fraud include: demanding full payment upfront; no written contract; no Texas contractor license; using high-pressure tactics; claiming to be FEMA-affiliated (FEMA does NOT endorse private contractors). Legitimate FEMA Individual Assistance programs do not charge application fees. FEMA IA registration is NOT yet open for Nueces County — anyone charging fees to register for FEMA assistance is committing fraud. Report fraud to the OAG Consumer Protection Hotline at (800) 621-0508 or the FEMA Disaster Fraud Hotline at 1-866-720-5721. Texas OAG has opened a price gouging investigation in Nueces County.

nodes.label: Citywide boil-water notice issued; bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes
nodes.statement: Citywide boil-water notice issued; bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes; water distribution sites open.

nodes.label: Because of the oil, the Texas Department of State Health Services closes shellfi
nodes.statement: Because of the oil, the Texas Department of State Health Services closes shellfish harvesting and Texas Parks and Wildlife closes fishing in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

nodes.label: A federal major disaster declaration for Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counti
nodes.statement: A federal major disaster declaration for Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties covers debris removal and emergency protective measures; FEMA says aid to households (Individual Assistance) depends on joint damage assessments now under way.

nodes.label: FEMA Region 6 today released preliminary damage assessment results based on the
nodes.statement: FEMA Region 6 today released preliminary damage assessment results based on the first systematic aerial drone survey of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area. A team of eight unmanned aircraft operated by Argus Aerial Systems under FEMA contract completed 180 square kilometers of coverage over residential and coastal zones between September 17 and 18. Based on automated structure analysis of approximately 847,000 image tiles, FEMA estimates between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael. These figures are preliminary and will be updated as the survey expands to additional zones, including the utility corridor and commercial districts. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park said: 'The aerial survey gives us the most comprehensive picture we have had in the first days after a Gulf Coast hurricane. We are sharing these results directly with Nueces County emergency management and the City of Corpus Christi to inform resource deployment.' Additional survey phases targeting utility infrastructure and the Port of Corpus Christi are scheduled to begin within the week.

nodes.label: UNIFIED COMMAND UPDATE — September 18, 2027: The Unified Command for the Inner H
nodes.statement: UNIFIED COMMAND UPDATE — September 18, 2027: The Unified Command for the Inner Harbor oil spill confirms heavy shoreline oiling along Nueces Bay. Oil released from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as Hurricane Rafael arrived was carried out of the ship channel by surge and wind; sheen covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. A TCEQ water quality station in Nueces Bay recorded petroleum hydrocarbon levels of 2.1 mg/L this afternoon. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists and personnel from the Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue have documented 41 oiled birds along the Nueces Bay shoreline, including brown pelicans and laughing gulls. Wildlife rescue operations are underway. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife has closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services has closed shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, effective immediately and until further notice. Additional containment boom is being placed at the Nueces Bay Causeway channel. The Coast Guard expects to issue its formal responsible-party designation within 72 hours. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

nodes.label: City warns employees and residents about phishing emails impersonating a disaste
nodes.statement: City warns employees and residents about phishing emails impersonating a disaster-aid portal.

nodes.label: Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor
nodes.statement: Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor and Coast Guard Sector Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han announced today that mass rescue operations in the Corpus Christi area have concluded, with 1,427 confirmed rescues over five days. The operation involved 34 coordinated teams at peak, including US Coast Guard, Texas Task Force 1, Corpus Christi Fire Department, Nueces County Sheriff Search and Rescue, and 87 credentialed civilian boat operators. Search teams recovered two bodies during the operation, both occupants of a submerged vehicle on Violet Road; the county's confirmed storm death toll stands at 23. Chief Vasquez-Okafor praised the performance of contracted UAS operators whose thermal imaging capabilities enabled the identification of survivors in darkness and debris. Commander Ostrowski-Han noted that this was the largest helicopter hoist rescue operation in Corpus Christi history. Remaining SAR resources will transition to welfare check mode; residents who have not yet been contacted by a welfare check team should call 211.

nodes.label: Coast Guard says investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access
nodes.statement: Coast Guard says investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems; federal cyber teams assisting.

nodes.label: NAS Corpus Christi says it is aware of drone reports and working with authoritie
nodes.statement: NAS Corpus Christi says it is aware of drone reports and working with authorities; no impact to operations.

nodes.label: Wastewater testing shows a norovirus signal; stomach illness visits rising.
nodes.statement: Wastewater testing shows a norovirus signal; stomach illness visits rising.

nodes.statement: Training aircraft begin returning to NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville.

nodes.label: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that marine inspect
nodes.statement: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that marine inspectors and pollution investigators completed inspections aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth yesterday, September 19, 2027. Both crews are safe. Both vessels remain moored under a Captain of the Port order and will not move until the investigation and the owners' obligations under federal oil spill law are addressed. Investigators documented the condition of the cargo systems on both ships and are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems, with federal cyber teams assisting. The Coast Guard will not characterize the cause of the release while the investigation is open. The oil spill response continues, with containment boom deployed along affected shoreline in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

nodes.label: The US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has submitted its formal Incident Summa
nodes.statement: The US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has submitted its formal Incident Summary Report for Operation Rafael SAR (ISR-2027-CC-004) to Coast Guard District 8. The report certifies 1,427 total rescues: 341 by helicopter hoist, 1,041 by surface vessel (Coast Guard, state, and civilian), and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts. The report notes that contracted unmanned aerial system operators provided 112 thermal imaging annotations directly used to coordinate surface rescue operations. The Coast Guard thanks the community of Corpus Christi and all mutual-aid partners for their outstanding response. A formal after-action review will be conducted within 90 days.

nodes.label: RESPONSIBLE PARTIES DESIGNATED — September 21, 2027: The U.S. Coast Guard, as Fe
nodes.statement: RESPONSIBLE PARTIES DESIGNATED — September 21, 2027: The U.S. Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator for the September 14 Inner Harbor oil release, has formally designated the owners of the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as responsible parties under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. Oil fingerprint analysis by the Coast Guard confirms that oil samples collected in the Inner Harbor, Corpus Christi Bay and Nueces Bay match the crude oil cargoes aboard the two vessels. The owners have been issued Notices of Federal Interest and are required to fund cleanup and to set up a process for damage claims. The estimated discharge remains about 9,000 barrels of crude oil. To keep response contractors working without interruption, the Coast Guard has opened the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund with an initial ceiling of $4.2 million, to be recovered from the responsible parties. The designation assigns financial responsibility for the response; it is not a finding on the cause of the release, which remains under investigation. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

nodes.label: ER visits for stomach illness up about 180% over normal; hallway beds in use.
nodes.statement: ER visits for stomach illness up about 180% over normal; hallway beds in use.

nodes.label: Brightwake Marine Systems says its remote-maintenance credentials were misused;
nodes.statement: Brightwake Marine Systems says its remote-maintenance credentials were misused; it revoked all remote access and is cooperating.

nodes.label: FEMA's Hurricane Rafael information line is now available in Spanish. Beginning
nodes.statement: FEMA's Hurricane Rafael information line is now available in Spanish. Beginning today, callers to 1-800-621-3362 may press 2 for Spanish-language assistance. Bilingual operators are staffed daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Spanish-language disaster information has also been posted online. The information line does not register households for aid: Individual Assistance has not been approved for Hurricane Rafael, and FEMA will announce it, and how to register, if that changes. For residents who need in-person help, FEMA and county staff are available at Richard King High School and Del Mar College East Campus.

nodes.statement: FBI confirms it is investigating drone reports near the air station.

nodes.statement: County awards a $14.2 million sole-source emergency debris contract to Vantorra Restoration LLC.

nodes.label: Utility says damaged plant pumps need replacement parts; temporary pumps limit c
nodes.statement: Utility says damaged plant pumps need replacement parts; temporary pumps limit capacity.

nodes.label: Coastline Public Radio has learned from Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Ce
nodes.statement: Coastline Public Radio has learned from Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center dispatch records, obtained through a public records request, that 23 calls from unregistered prepaid phones since September 21 reported emergencies at addresses in northwest and central Corpus Christi near two utility sites — at least eleven of them describing trapped residents — but responders found no one and no emergency at any of those locations. Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor of the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center confirmed the unfounded calls, said the center had flagged the cluster internally and had referred the information to its law enforcement partners. No suspects have been identified.

nodes.label: No new drone sightings reported after ten days.
nodes.statement: No new drone sightings reported after ten days.

nodes.label: A claims center run for the tankers' owners opens for spill cleanup and property
nodes.statement: A claims center run for the tankers' owners opens for spill cleanup and property damage claims, as federal oil spill law requires.

nodes.label: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center is experiencing a significant i
nodes.statement: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center is experiencing a significant increase in calls related to today's boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss urges residents with water safety questions to call the newly established NuecesInfoLine at 361-826-INFO rather than 911. '911 is for life-threatening emergencies only,' Director Escamilla-Voss said. 'The NuecesInfoLine has operators available to answer your questions about the boil water notice, water distribution sites, and when water service is expected to be restored — please use that number and keep 911 available for people whose lives are in danger.' The NuecesInfoLine is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Information is also available in Spanish by pressing 2. Water distribution sites are open at the Tuloso-Midway High School gym, the Woodlawn Community Center, and Cefe Valenzuela Park; hours and addresses are listed at the City of Corpus Christi emergency management website.

nodes.label: BOIL WATER NOTICE — Districts 3 and 4. Effective immediately, all residents and
nodes.statement: BOIL WATER NOTICE — Districts 3 and 4. Effective immediately, all residents and businesses served by the City of Corpus Christi water system in Water Districts 3 and 4 (ZIP codes 78401, 78405, 78407, 78408, 78416 and 78417) are advised to boil all water used for drinking, cooking, and making ice. This notice is issued due to low system pressure in these districts following Hurricane Rafael damage to distribution infrastructure. To make water safe: bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes before use. This notice affects approximately 48,000 residents. Updates will be issued through the City's emergency notification system, local television and local radio. For more information call 361-826-1600.

nodes.label: BOIL WATER NOTICE — September 26, 2027 5:30 PM CDT: THE COASTAL BEND POWER AND W
nodes.statement: BOIL WATER NOTICE — September 26, 2027 5:30 PM CDT: THE COASTAL BEND POWER AND WATER AUTHORITY HAS ISSUED A BOIL WATER NOTICE FOR DISTRICTS 3 AND 4 OF THE CORPUS CHRISTI WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM. THIS NOTICE AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY 48,000 RESIDENTS. DUE TO LOW WATER PRESSURE AND DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM DISRUPTIONS, ALL TAP WATER MUST BE BOILED BEFORE USE FOR DRINKING, COOKING, MAKING ICE, OR BRUSHING TEETH. BRING WATER TO A ROLLING BOIL FOR TWO MINUTES BEFORE USE. BOTTLED WATER DISTRIBUTION SITES ARE OPERATING AT TULOSO-MIDWAY HIGH SCHOOL GYM, WOODLAWN COMMUNITY CENTER, AND CEFE VALENZUELA PARK. DISTRICTS 3 AND 4 INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING ZIP CODES: 78401, 78405, 78407, 78408, 78416, 78417. FOR INFORMATION CALL CBPWA AT (361) 555-0280. AVISO DE AGUA A HERVIR: La version en espanol de este aviso se distribuira por separado. [WEA: BOIL WATER NOTICE Districts 3-4 Corpus Christi. Boil all tap water before use. Bottled water: Tuloso-Midway HS, Woodlawn Ctr, Cefe Valenzuela Park. CBPWA (361)555-0280]

nodes.label: The City of Corpus Christi Water Department has issued a boil water notice for D
nodes.statement: The City of Corpus Christi Water Department has issued a boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4, effective immediately. Low water pressure in the distribution system serving the two districts — a consequence of storm damage to treatment and pumping infrastructure — means that contamination cannot be ruled out. Approximately 48,000 residents are affected. All tap water must be brought to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking or cooking until further notice.

nodes.label: Spanish-speaking residents of Districts 3 and 4 did not receive the city's boil-
nodes.statement: Spanish-speaking residents of Districts 3 and 4 did not receive the city's boil-water notice until more than 12 hours after English-language alerts went out Sunday evening, the Bayside Ledger has confirmed. The notice, issued at 5:30 p.m. Sunday, reached KNCB Coastal Bend Radio — the primary news source for an estimated 34,000 Spanish-speaking listeners in Corpus Christi — only at 6:03 Monday morning. 'We received the official notice from the city this morning,' KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega said Monday. 'By then many of our listeners had already been using untreated water overnight.' Nueces County Office of Emergency Management spokesperson Cassandra Trejo-Morales confirmed the delay, attributing it to reduced staffing at the county's translation contractor, Nueces County Language Access Services. 'We are reviewing what happened and what can be done differently,' Trejo-Morales said. The boil-water notice covers approximately 48,000 residents and remained in effect as of press time.

nodes.label: Stomach illness visits begin to ease.
nodes.statement: Stomach illness visits begin to ease.

nodes.label: Residents in low-income neighborhoods near the bay report waiting days for help
nodes.statement: Residents in low-income neighborhoods near the bay report waiting days for help after the storm.

nodes.label: Restoration crews working in Corpus Christi have encountered cascading substatio
nodes.statement: Restoration crews working in Corpus Christi have encountered cascading substation failures in the northwest and central districts that are extending the recovery timeline beyond initial estimates. Crews are on-site at two facilities to investigate protective relay conditions exacerbated by storm debris. We expect the final 32,000 affected customers in those areas to be restored within 7 to 10 days. We appreciate their patience.

nodes.label: FEMA's Mitigation Assessment Team today released the Phase 2 Utility Infrastruct
nodes.statement: FEMA's Mitigation Assessment Team today released the Phase 2 Utility Infrastructure Aerial Survey Summary for the Corpus Christi Hurricane Rafael response. The survey, completed over September 23 through 26, covered 23 utility infrastructure sites including five CBPWA electrical substations, the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, four pumping stations, and nine telecommunications relay facilities. The assessment found visible storm damage at 14 of the 23 sites, with the O.N. Stevens plant sustaining moderate roof damage to the C-pump station. The report identifies two CBPWA substations — Harbor View and Crosstown — as requiring follow-up engineering inspection due to equipment configurations observed in the imagery. Texas Division of Emergency Management Infrastructure Division Chief Rafael Montoya-Chen said: 'The aerial survey has given engineers a roadmap so that when crews reach those sites, they know what to look for and can prioritize the most critical restoration steps.' The full Phase 2 imagery set is available to credentialed government users through the FEMA GeoPlatform.

nodes.label: The Federal Aviation Administration and US Customs and Border Protection Air and
nodes.statement: The Federal Aviation Administration and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations today confirmed that investigators have identified multiple incidents of unauthorized unmanned aircraft system operations in the Corpus Christi area during the period preceding Hurricane Rafael. The aircraft operated without required FAA authorizations and were detected through a combination of radar and electronic sensor records. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) and the US Coast Guard are coordinating with the FAA and appropriate law enforcement agencies. Due to the ongoing nature of the investigation, no additional details about the number, location, or timing of the incidents can be released at this time. CBP and FAA jointly urge any members of the public with information about unauthorized drone operations in the Corpus Christi area between September 4 and September 12, 2027, to contact the FBI field office at 361-888-3111.

nodes.label: CONTRACTOR FRAUD ALERT — September 29, 2027: The Texas Department of Public Safe
nodes.statement: CONTRACTOR FRAUD ALERT — September 29, 2027: The Texas Department of Public Safety is issuing an urgent consumer alert following more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water damage contractors in the Corpus Christi area since Hurricane Rafael. Residents in Districts 3 and 4, particularly those affected by flooding and water damage from the storm, are most at risk. Specific complaints include contractors charging for water extraction, mold remediation, and drywall repair at prices 3 to 5 times above normal market rates; charging for services never performed; using forged insurance adjuster documentation; and requesting victims sign over assignment-of-benefits rights to allow direct billing to insurance carriers without homeowner review. DPS urges residents to: verify contractor license at license.state.tx.us; get minimum three written estimates; never sign assignment-of-benefits without reading the full document; pay only after work is completed and inspected. Any resident who believes they have been victimized should contact Texas DPS at (512) 424-2000 or local law enforcement. This warning applies to all contractors, including those offering emergency water damage restoration services.

nodes.label: Threat researcher finds rumor posts were coordinated across about 40 accounts an
nodes.statement: Threat researcher finds rumor posts were coordinated across about 40 accounts and linked to the same lookalike aid site used in phishing emails (aid-help-portal.example).

nodes.label: Gulfwater Maritime Report has confirmed with sources familiar with the investiga
nodes.statement: Gulfwater Maritime Report has confirmed with sources familiar with the investigation that federal authorities are examining whether commercial drones conducted surveillance flights over the Port of Corpus Christi and at least one local power utility facility in the days before Hurricane Rafael. Sources say the flights were detected through radar records maintained by the Coast Guard. No organization has claimed responsibility. The timing of the flights — the week before Hurricane Rafael landfall — has drawn attention from investigators given subsequent damage to critical infrastructure during and after the storm. The FBI has asked for public tips.

nodes.label: HEALTH ADVISORY: Waterborne Disease Cluster — Districts 3 and 4. The Corpus Chri
nodes.statement: HEALTH ADVISORY: Waterborne Disease Cluster — Districts 3 and 4. The Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District is investigating an elevated number of cases of acute gastrointestinal illness, including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps, among residents of Water Districts 3 and 4. As of today, Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center have treated more than 600 patients with these symptoms since September 29, the majority of whom reside in Districts 3 and 4. Laboratory tests have confirmed the presence of Cryptosporidium and Giardia — waterborne parasites — in multiple patient samples. These findings are consistent with consumption of untreated water. All residents in Districts 3 and 4 must continue to boil all water used for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, and making ice until further notice. Boil water vigorously for two minutes before use. If you are experiencing severe dehydration, bloody diarrhea, or are immunocompromised, seek emergency medical care immediately. Additional information will be provided as the investigation continues. For questions, call the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District line: 361-826-7200.

nodes.label: Pump parts delayed: the supplier's local warehouse flooded and parts are shippin
nodes.statement: Pump parts delayed: the supplier's local warehouse flooded and parts are shipping from out of state.

nodes.label: Federal contract records show a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract for NAS Cor
nodes.statement: Federal contract records show a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract for NAS Corpus Christi to Quellmar Fuel Partners after the station's regular supplier flooded.

nodes.label: CLEANUP MILESTONE — October 4, 2027: Unified Command announces that the main oil
nodes.statement: CLEANUP MILESTONE — October 4, 2027: Unified Command announces that the main oil slick from the September 14 Inner Harbor discharge is contained. Primary skimming operations have concluded with recovery of approximately 142,000 gallons of oil-water mixture. TCEQ monitoring readings in Corpus Christi Bay have declined to an average of 0.40 milligrams per liter, down from a peak of 3.4 mg/L recorded on September 17. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant raw water intake has returned to below the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold and is operating normally. Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue reports 340 oiled birds documented through today; 198 birds have been successfully rehabilitated and released. Shoreline cleanup operations in Nueces Bay are ongoing, with hand crews working approximately 6.4 kilometers of affected shoreline. The response is moving from emergency containment to shoreline cleanup. Fishing and shellfish harvesting closures in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays remain in effect pending state testing. Joint Information Center: (361) 555-0147.

nodes.label: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has confirmed that it is investigating an
nodes.statement: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has confirmed that it is investigating anomalous access to internal network systems that may have occurred during the Hurricane Rafael response period. CBPWA's Security Operations Center identified unusual access patterns in network logs and has opened a formal security review in coordination with Vantage Security Systems, our SIEM and security technology partner. At this time there is no indication that customer data has been affected. CBPWA is working closely with relevant federal and state agencies. Additional information will be provided as the investigation progresses. CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna is leading the investigation.

nodes.label: Fishing closure extended; respiratory complaints near shorelines easing.
nodes.statement: Fishing closure extended; respiratory complaints near shorelines easing.

nodes.label: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bure
nodes.statement: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation today announced a joint investigation into anomalous activity affecting industrial control systems at a coastal electric utility in Texas during the Hurricane Rafael response period. The activity was identified during routine review of utility incident reports submitted under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act. CISA and FBI are working with the affected utility and state partners to assess the scope, origin, and impact of the activity. No attribution has been made at this time. Utilities in the Gulf Coast region are encouraged to review and implement CISA's operational technology security guidelines and report anomalous ICS activity through the CISA 24/7 operations center. This investigation is ongoing and additional information will be provided as appropriate.

nodes.label: JOINT STATEMENT — October 5, 2027: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Joint
nodes.statement: JOINT STATEMENT — October 5, 2027: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Joint Field Office and the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority are issuing this statement regarding the extended power outages affecting Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael. While the initial power outages were caused by wind and storm surge damage to the CBPWA transmission and distribution network, investigators from the federal government and CBPWA have determined that the duration of outages in certain districts was extended by deliberate interference with utility control systems beyond what storm damage alone would have caused. This determination was made following a technical review of utility operational data by federal investigators. The investigation is ongoing. CBPWA has implemented enhanced security measures for its control systems and is working with federal partners to prevent future incidents. No decision has been made on whether residents who experienced prolonged outages will be eligible for additional disaster assistance. Power has been restored to most customers; restoration in parts of northwest and central Corpus Christi is continuing while relay inspection and repair are completed. CBPWA urges any customer with information relevant to this investigation to contact the FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency at (361) 555-0100.

nodes.label: The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Sec
nodes.statement: The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency are investigating unauthorized access to control systems at a Corpus Christi utility. Texas Cyber Command has been activated to assist. The Governor has directed all critical infrastructure operators in the state to review remote-access security procedures and report any anomalies to CISA. This investigation is active and ongoing; no further operational details will be released at this time.

nodes.label: The Texas Division of Emergency Management today released a first after-action s
nodes.statement: The Texas Division of Emergency Management today released a first after-action snapshot on public communications during Hurricane Rafael. It notes 'observed delays in Spanish-language alert distribution' but gives no figures and makes no recommendations. Separately, a local chapter of the League of United Latin American Citizens filed a complaint with the state citing its limited-English-proficiency plan and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. KNCB Coastal Bend Radio read the complaint on the air.

nodes.label: The Texas Department of State Health Services has completed a preliminary invest
nodes.statement: The Texas Department of State Health Services has completed a preliminary investigation into the waterborne disease outbreak affecting Corpus Christi Water Districts 3 and 4. DSHS has confirmed that Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia are the causative agents of the outbreak. Both pathogens are transmitted exclusively through contaminated water. The investigation determined that exposure occurred during the period of low water pressure in Districts 3 and 4 following Hurricane Rafael, consistent with the Boil Water Notice issued by the City of Corpus Christi on September 26, 2027. DSHS is coordinating with the City of Corpus Christi, Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority, and the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District on the ongoing public health response. The Boil Water Notice for Districts 3 and 4 remains in effect. Residents should continue to boil all water before consumption. DSHS advises all immunocompromised individuals, infants, and elderly residents in the affected area to contact their healthcare provider if they have experienced any gastrointestinal symptoms.

nodes.label: CISA has issued Emergency Directive 27-02 directing all federal agencies operati
nodes.statement: CISA has issued Emergency Directive 27-02 directing all federal agencies operating industrial control systems to audit remote-access credentials and configuration change logs within 72 hours. The directive follows a confirmed ICS incident at a Texas utility in which a threat actor gained access via compromised remote-access credentials and made unauthorized changes to operational technology systems. Owners and operators of critical infrastructure are strongly encouraged to review CISA Advisory AA27-266A for indicators and mitigations.

nodes.label: Household damage assessments are slowed by spill-zone access limits, flooded roa
nodes.statement: Household damage assessments are slowed by spill-zone access limits, flooded roads and the scale of damage; the state formally asks FEMA to add Individual Assistance; advocates say families without savings are waiting.

nodes.label: Governor has amended the existing Hurricane Rafael disaster declaration to inclu
nodes.statement: Governor has amended the existing Hurricane Rafael disaster declaration to include a cyber emergency component covering Corpus Christi utility infrastructure. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has deployed a cybersecurity rapid response team to assist local and state authorities. The affected utility has isolated its control systems as a precautionary measure; field crews are managing operations manually. The Governor's office emphasized that the water supply remains safe for boiled use and that electric restoration continues.

nodes.label: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today reported that Hurricane R
nodes.statement: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today reported that Hurricane Rafael emergency call volume has returned to near-normal levels, with 380 calls received yesterday — approaching the pre-storm daily baseline of 310 calls. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss said the center is beginning a transition back to normal staffing over the next two weeks. 'Our dispatchers have shown extraordinary dedication over the past four weeks. The scale and duration of this response was unprecedented for our center, and I am incredibly proud of every person who answered calls, coordinated rescues, and kept working through the most demanding conditions I have seen in my career.' Director Escamilla-Voss noted that CBECC handled more than 44,200 calls in the four weeks after landfall, about five times the normal volume. The center is retaining all call records and audio as part of its standard after-action review process. Mutual aid units from San Patricio and Bee County will begin scaling back their support beginning October 14.

nodes.label: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has taken precautionary steps to isolate
nodes.statement: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has taken precautionary steps to isolate portions of its operational technology network following the identification of unauthorized access to network systems. These measures are being taken as part of an ongoing security investigation. The isolation is expected to cause no disruption to power or water service for CBPWA customers. CBPWA is cooperating with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and other relevant authorities. CBPWA emphasizes that the investigation is ongoing and no conclusions should be drawn about the nature or origin of the access at this time.

nodes.label: Ship channel partly reopens; spill decontamination keeps the inner channel restr
nodes.statement: Ship channel partly reopens; spill decontamination keeps the inner channel restricted; anchorage backlog delays relief cargo including MV Gulf Provider.

nodes.label: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority announced today that the Corpus Christi Shi
nodes.statement: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority announced today that the Corpus Christi Ship Channel has partly reopened to commercial traffic, 30 days after Hurricane Rafael closed it. The Coast Guard cleared the outer and bay reaches of the channel after surveys of channel depth and aids to navigation. The inner channel remains restricted while vessels and berths affected by the Inner Harbor oil spill are decontaminated; no date has been set for lifting that restriction. Ships waiting at the offshore anchorage will be brought in by priority, and the backlog will delay some cargo, including relief shipments. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves said: 'We are grateful for the patience of our customers and maritime partners. The port team, together with the Coast Guard, NOAA and our contractor crews, worked extraordinary hours to restore safe navigation after one of the most demanding storm responses in our history.' Six port security cameras along the Inner Harbor remain offline pending replacement parts. The Coast Guard investigation into the tanker oil release remains open.

nodes.label: BOIL WATER NOTICES REMAIN IN EFFECT — weekly update. / LOS AVISOS DE HERVIR AGUA
nodes.statement: BOIL WATER NOTICES REMAIN IN EFFECT — weekly update. / LOS AVISOS DE HERVIR AGUA SIGUEN VIGENTES — actualización semanal. The Corpus Christi Water Department announces that the citywide boil water notice issued September 18, 2027 and the Boil Water Notice issued September 26, 2027 for Water Districts 3 and 4 both remain in effect as of 9:00 a.m. today, October 14, 2027. Replacement pump parts for the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant have not yet arrived, and neither notice can be lifted until repairs are complete and water quality testing meets all state and federal standards. Continue to bring water to a rolling boil before drinking, cooking, making ice or brushing teeth. This update is being released in English and Spanish at the same time. / La Ciudad de Corpus Christi anuncia que el aviso de hervir agua para toda la ciudad, emitido el 18 de septiembre de 2027, y el aviso emitido el 26 de septiembre de 2027 para los Distritos de Agua 3 y 4 siguen vigentes a las 9:00 a.m. de hoy, 14 de octubre de 2027. Las piezas de repuesto para las bombas de la planta O.N. Stevens aún no han llegado. Siga hirviendo el agua antes de beberla, cocinar, hacer hielo o cepillarse los dientes. Este aviso se publica en inglés y en español al mismo tiempo.

nodes.label: DISASTER CLAIMS SURGE UPDATE — October 14, 2027: The Texas Department of Insuran
nodes.statement: DISASTER CLAIMS SURGE UPDATE — October 14, 2027: The Texas Department of Insurance and the Insurance Council of Texas report that Hurricane Rafael has generated approximately 187,000 property insurance claims across Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties as of October 14, representing an estimated $2.1 billion in insured losses. This ranks as the second-largest coastal insured loss event in Texas since Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Claims volume in the Corpus Christi metropolitan area exceeds industry catastrophe response models by approximately 23 percent. TDI has activated its Disaster Response Team and deployed 12 field claim examiners. The department notes an elevated pattern of large commercial property claims in Districts 3-5 that is under review. Adjusters are reporting difficulty verifying pre-storm property values in certain commercial portfolios. Homeowners and commercial property owners are reminded that Texas law requires insurers to acknowledge claims within 15 days and pay or deny within 15 business days of receiving all claim documentation. Residents experiencing claim delays should contact TDI at (800) 252-3439. TDI is tracking contractor fraud complaints and coordinating with the Texas DPS.

nodes.label: TDI ACTIVATES CLAIMS FRAUD TASK FORCE — October 14, 2027: Texas Department of In
nodes.statement: TDI ACTIVATES CLAIMS FRAUD TASK FORCE — October 14, 2027: Texas Department of Insurance Commissioner announces the activation of a Disaster Claims Fraud Task Force for Nueces County following Hurricane Rafael. The task force, operating in coordination with the FBI and Texas DPS, will focus on detecting and preventing fraudulent insurance claims arising from the storm. TDI has identified patterns of concern including clusters of large commercial property claims with similar damage narratives, inflated pre-storm appraisals, and claims for total losses on properties that sustained only partial damage. TDI emphasizes that filing a fraudulent insurance claim is a third-degree felony in Texas, punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and fines up to $10,000. Insurers are reminded of their obligation to refer suspected fraud to TDI's Fraud Unit. TDI is working with the Insurance Council of Texas to establish a Nueces County claims database to identify duplicate and suspicious claims across carriers. Legitimate policyholders are encouraged to cooperate with claim investigations and to report any third party who pressured them into filing inflated claims.

nodes.label: The Texas Division of Emergency Management, working with federal partners, has i
nodes.statement: The Texas Division of Emergency Management, working with federal partners, has identified and referred to law enforcement a network of social media accounts that disseminated false public safety information during Hurricane Rafael. The accounts distributed incorrect evacuation shelter locations, false road closure information, and misleading content about utility restoration and federal investigations. TDEM's social media monitoring tool, Coastal Alert, detected anomalous posting behavior consistent with coordinated inauthentic behavior. TDEM has referred account information to the FBI and has coordinated with social media platforms on account review. Members of the public who encountered false shelter or evacuation information during the Rafael response are asked to report it to TDEM's public information line at 512-424-2208. TDEM reminds the public to verify emergency information through official sources: NuecesCountyOEM.org, 2-1-1 Texas, and local broadcast stations designated in the Corpus Christi Emergency Alert System.

nodes.label: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
nodes.statement: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority today announced a joint counter-unmanned aircraft initiative for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor, following a recommendation in the FAA-CBP joint report on pre-storm unauthorized drone activity. The initiative will deploy an RF-sensing detection and direction-finding network at multiple sites across the port and utility infrastructure corridor, operated in coordination with the FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations. Sentinel Airspace Inc. has been selected as the technology provider following a competitive evaluation. The network is expected to be operational within 90 days. Port Director Marcus Obianwu-Kelley and CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna jointly signed the agreement.

nodes.label: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority is pleased to announce that the final 3,2
nodes.statement: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority is pleased to announce that the final 3,200 customers in northwest Corpus Christi have been restored to electric service following extensive relay inspection, repair, and hardening work by our crews and ERCOT partners. All Corpus Christi load zones are now above 99 percent restoration. We thank residents for their patience during this extended recovery period.

nodes.statement: Replacement pump parts arrive at O.N. Stevens.

nodes.label: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure
nodes.statement: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency have notified the public that CBPWA has completed an initial phase of remediation following a confirmed security incident affecting CBPWA's industrial control system network. CBPWA's security monitoring systems have returned to normal operational status. No customer data was exfiltrated. CISA has issued an ICS advisory (ICS-CERT-2027-CC-00441) to the broader critical infrastructure community regarding the attack techniques observed. CBPWA is conducting a comprehensive post-incident review and will implement additional security hardening measures identified during the investigation.

nodes.label: Public AIS data shows the fishing vessel FV Pelican Ridge's identity broadcastin
nodes.statement: Public AIS data shows the fishing vessel FV Pelican Ridge's identity broadcasting off Port Aransas overnight Oct. 14-15, the night after the channel partly reopened while the same vessel reported a position about 600 nautical miles away; an analyst calls it consistent with identity spoofing.

nodes.label: Two major social media platforms announced Friday the removal of 847 accounts en
nodes.statement: Two major social media platforms announced Friday the removal of 847 accounts engaged in coordinated inauthentic behavior related to Hurricane Rafael public safety communications. The companies said the accounts had spread false evacuation shelter locations, fabricated road closure reports, and promoted misleading claims about the cause of extended power outages in Corpus Christi. The platforms said the accounts showed 'clear indicators of artificial coordination' including synchronized posting times, shared infrastructure, and near-identical content across different handles. The joint announcement followed referrals from the Texas Division of Emergency Management and the FBI's Cyber Division. Neither platform attributed the network to a specific actor or government. Texas Attorney General spokesperson Brandon Lacey-Rhinehart said the state was 'continuing to investigate the origin and intent of this coordinated effort to undermine public safety during a natural disaster.' The discovery of the false shelter posts is of particular concern: Nueces County OEM confirmed that at least 23 residents called the county 211 line on the day before landfall asking about Zavala Elementary as a shelter location, based on social media posts that have since been removed.

nodes.statement: Citywide boil-water notice lifted after pump repairs and testing; Districts 3 and 4 remain under their separate notice until testing there is complete.

nodes.statement: Pilots report GPS interference within about 40 miles of Corpus Christi; FAA issues a notice; relief flights continue using backup navigation.

nodes.label: The Office of the Texas Attorney General today issued a consumer advisory warnin
nodes.statement: The Office of the Texas Attorney General today issued a consumer advisory warning Texans about misinformation campaigns targeting emergency communications during natural disasters. During Hurricane Rafael, coordinated social media accounts posted false information including incorrect evacuation shelter addresses, fabricated road closure reports, and misleading claims about the causes of utility outages in the Corpus Christi area. The OAG advises Texans to: verify emergency information only through official government websites and designated emergency broadcast stations; report suspected misinformation to local emergency management or through the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3.gov); and be cautious of social media accounts with limited post history that suddenly begin posting high volumes of local emergency content. The OAG is cooperating with the FBI's ongoing investigation into the organized distribution of false public safety information during the Rafael response period.

nodes.label: The boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 has been lifted, effective 11:00 AM
nodes.statement: The boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 has been lifted, effective 11:00 AM today. Water pressure at all test points in the two districts has been confirmed above 40 psi and water quality testing has met all TCEQ standards. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant is operating at full capacity. Residents may resume normal tap water use. The City thanks residents for their cooperation during the 30-day notice period.

nodes.label: FEMA Region 6 announced today the completion of the Hurricane Rafael Aerial Asse
nodes.statement: FEMA Region 6 announced today the completion of the Hurricane Rafael Aerial Assessment Program, the most comprehensive post-storm aerial survey conducted in the Texas Gulf Coast region. From a pre-storm baseline on September 12 through October 29, federal, state, and contracted aerial assets generated more than 6.2 million georeferenced image tiles covering 183 square kilometers of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area. The imagery archive spans all phases of the disaster cycle from pre-storm baseline through active recovery. Beginning today, downsampled imagery from Phase 1 and Phase 2 surveys is publicly available through the FEMA OpenData portal for use by academic researchers, local governments, and community organizations engaged in recovery planning. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park stated: 'This imagery archive is a resource that will support not just today's recovery, but future preparedness for the entire Texas Gulf Coast. We are grateful to NOAA, the Texas Army National Guard, and our contracted partners for executing this mission under difficult post-storm conditions.' Requests for access to full-resolution imagery should be directed to FEMA Region 6 Geospatial Programs at the contact listed below.

nodes.label: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today formally closed its Hurri
nodes.statement: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today formally closed its Hurricane Rafael surge response posture and returned to standard staffing levels. Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss announced that CBECC has established a partnership with Nueces County Information Technology to preserve the call record archive from landfall through October 29 for training and after-action analysis purposes. The archive covers more than 56,000 calls in English and Spanish and represents the most complete 911 call record ever retained for a Gulf Coast storm response. Director Escamilla-Voss also announced a new 911 abuse reporting tip line, 1-800-NUECES-9, for residents to report suspected false emergency reports. 'During any major emergency, bad actors sometimes attempt to abuse the emergency communications system to divert rescuers,' said Escamilla-Voss. 'We take this seriously, and we ask the public to help us protect the integrity of 911 by reporting suspected abuse.' The NuecesInfoLine, opened during the boil-water notices, will close on Friday, November 5. CBECC thanks the residents of Districts 3 and 4 for their patience during the extended water notices.

nodes.label: KNCB Coastal Bend Radio news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega testified before the
nodes.statement: KNCB Coastal Bend Radio news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega testified before the Nueces County Commissioners Court today regarding gaps in bilingual emergency communications during Hurricane Rafael. Fuentes-Vega presented broadcast logs documenting delays between English and Spanish public alerts across four alert categories during the Rafael response: mandatory evacuation orders (2 hours 47 minutes), shelter-in-place guidance (7 hours 52 minutes), boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (12 hours 33 minutes), and power restoration status announcements (average 9 hours 11 minutes). The average delay across all categories was 8 hours 6 minutes. Commissioners voted 4–1 to direct the county's Office of Emergency Management to issue a new Request for Proposals for language access services requiring simultaneous multi-language alert release within 30 minutes for all life-safety notifications.

nodes.label: Sabal Energy Wire has obtained documents confirming that the prolonged power out
nodes.statement: Sabal Energy Wire has obtained documents confirming that the prolonged power outages affecting portions of Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael were partly attributable to unauthorized modifications to protective relay settings at two CBPWA substations. The modifications, discovered during a security investigation that began October 2nd, caused affected relay groups to tolerate fault currents above their designed trip thresholds, extending grid restoration timelines by an estimated 11 to 18 days. CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna declined to comment on specific findings, citing an ongoing investigation. CISA confirmed that ICS-CERT advisory ICS-2027-CC-00441 covers incidents of this type.

nodes.label: Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center today released the
nodes.statement: Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center today released their joint Hurricane Rafael Hospital Operations After-Action Report. The report documents the response of both facilities from September 11 through October 14, 2027. Combined, the two hospitals treated 4,217 hurricane-related patients over that period. The response involved two distinct patient surge waves: a trauma wave from landfall on September 14 through September 21, during which SRMC operated at up to 140% licensed bed capacity on generator power, and a waterborne disease cluster from September 29 through October 12, during which 1,820 patients were treated for Cryptosporidium and Giardia infection. The cluster was geographically concentrated in Water Districts 3 and 4. The report notes that early-cluster admissions disproportionately included patients from Spanish-dominant households, a pattern the report identifies as potentially related to the delay in Spanish-language boil-water notification. No patient deaths were directly attributable to the hospital surge response. The report recommends expanded generator diesel reserves, pre-positioned water testing capabilities, and enhanced multilingual patient communication protocols for future mass casualty and public health emergency events.

nodes.label: 60-DAY REMEDIATION ASSESSMENT — November 13, 2027: The Texas Commission on Envir
nodes.statement: 60-DAY REMEDIATION ASSESSMENT — November 13, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and EPA Region 6 have completed the 60-day remediation assessment for the Inner Harbor oil release (TCEQ Incident Case CC-ENV-2027-0916). Water quality monitoring shows Corpus Christi Bay total petroleum hydrocarbon concentrations have returned to 0.03 mg/L, below the TCEQ Class 2 surface water standard of 0.05 mg/L. Nueces Bay shoreline cleanup is 94 percent complete; minor tar ball accumulation persists on approximately 0.4 kilometers of shoreline near the Nueces Bay Causeway and will be addressed through the 2028 spring shoreline maintenance program. Raw-water intake readings at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant have remained below the hydrocarbon alert threshold for 52 consecutive days. The emergency response phase is hereby closed. Fishing and shellfish harvesting closures remain in effect until state testing supports reopening. Long-term ecological monitoring of Nueces Bay seagrass beds and oyster reef habitats will continue under a separate TCEQ Natural Resource Damage Assessment agreement with the owners of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay Total documented cleanup cost is $8.2 million. Wildlife rehabilitation costs of $0.9 million and estimated commercial fishing economic losses of $5.6 million are subject to Natural Resource Damage Assessment proceedings. This assessment has been transmitted to NOAA, USFWS, and Texas Parks and Wildlife for NRD purposes.

nodes.label: OPERATION SANDBAR — 14 ARRESTED IN HURRICANE RAFAEL DISASTER FRAUD SCHEME — Dece
nodes.statement: OPERATION SANDBAR — 14 ARRESTED IN HURRICANE RAFAEL DISASTER FRAUD SCHEME — December 13, 2027: The Federal Bureau of Investigation Houston Division, FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency, and the Texas Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division today announced 14 arrests in connection with a large-scale disaster fraud scheme that targeted federal disaster assistance programs and private insurers following Hurricane Rafael. The defendants, led by Corpus Christi resident Renaldo Carver-Mossbach, 44, are accused of fraudulently inflating insurance values on 230 properties before the storm and subsequently filing 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications claiming damage that did not occur or was dramatically overstated. Total alleged fraud losses exceed $23 million. Property management company Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC, water damage restoration firm FastDry Coastal LLC, and appraisal firm Duvall and Sons Property Consultants are named in the complaint. The defendants face federal charges of wire fraud, mail fraud, false statements to a federal agency, and conspiracy, carrying maximum penalties of 20 to 30 years in federal prison. FEMA has suspended 94 Individual Assistance awards pending investigation and is contacting affected applicants whose claims were filed without their knowledge. Texas DPS urges any resident who engaged with FastDry Coastal LLC or Landmark Pacific Holdings representatives after the storm to contact the Operation Sandbar tip line at (361) 555-0199.

nodes.label: Station's suspended emergency fuel supplier named in federal court filing
nodes.dek: A civil forfeiture filing says Quellmar Fuel Partners, which the Navy suspended in November, shares an offshore owner with a county debris contractor.

nodes.label: Reabren parte de las zonas de pesca; ya hay unos 4,200 reclamos por el derrame / Fishing grounds partly reopen; about 4,200 spill claims filed
nodes.dek: Las agencias reabrieron lo que las pruebas permiten. Pescadores y dueños de terrenos en la orilla siguen esperando pagos. / Agencies reopened what testing supports; fishers and shoreline owners are still waiting on payments.

nodes.label: From a sole-source award to a forfeiture filing: the paper trail on two storm contractors
nodes.dek: In less than four months, two companies hired after Rafael went from emergency contracts to a federal filing naming a shared offshore owner. A timeline from the public record.

nodes.label: Inner Harbor spill: about 4,200 damage claims filed as bay fishing grounds partly reopen
nodes.dek: State agencies reopened part of the closed waters after testing. The claims count gives the first public measure of the spill's commercial reach.

nodes.label: Opinion: Finish the door-to-door work before the last chapter of Rafael is written
nodes.dek: An opinion column. A federal filing says millions in disaster aid were diverted. The neighborhoods that got the least still need someone to knock.

nodes.label: Port of Corpus Christi starts 2028 with an open channel and a longer to-do list
nodes.dek: Exports are flowing after two closures in a single fall. The port's spokesman says resilience and security will shape the year.

nodes.label: Rafael, four months on: four neighbors, four kinds of waiting
nodes.dek: A home health aide, a schoolteacher, a shrimper and a bait shop owner take stock as rebuilding continues and reviews of water, aid, port security and contracting go on.

nodes.label: Four months after Rafael, the reviews are under way. A pastor and a deckhand say what they'd ask
nodes.dek: Water, aid equity, port security and contracting are all under review. Two people who lived through the storm's hardest moments say what reviewers should hear.

nodes.label: Four months after Rafael: the Corpus Christi channel log, and the reviews still open
nodes.dek: Two closures, one partial reopening, one full sweep. The port is working normally, and the review of port security is one of several still under way.

nodes.label: Four Months After Rafael, Corpus Christi Is Rebuilding — and Reckoning
nodes.dek: On the four-month mark of Hurricane Rafael's landfall, the Bayside Ledger surveys what has been repaired, what has been reformed, and what still remains undone — through statistics, court records, and the voices of people who stayed.

nodes.label: Cuatro meses después de Rafael: lo que cambió, y lo que falta, para las familias hispanohablantes / Four months after Rafael: what changed, and what's still missing, for Spanish-speaking families
nodes.dek: La reconstrucción sigue, y también las revisiones del agua, la ayuda, la seguridad del puerto y los contratos. / Rebuilding continues, as do reviews of water, aid, port security and contracting.

nodes.label: Four months after Rafael: what the crude market learned about depending on one channel
nodes.dek: Exports are back and the anchorage is busy. An analyst says the lesson of the fall was not the storm but the share: about half of U.S. crude exports through a single entrance.

nodes.label: Four months after Rafael, a Texas energy hub rebuilds as investigators sort storm from sabotage
nodes.dek: Tankers are moving and most lights are on. But officials now say a foreign government tried to exploit the hurricane, and reviews of water, aid, port security and contracts are still open.

nodes.label: Four months after Rafael: a thank-you, and a to-do list for 2028
nodes.dek: A look back at what station and depot families carried this fall, what is still under review and six things to do before next hurricane season.

nodes.id: old:WQ-05 (Nueces River at Calallen - upstream gauge)
nodes.label: WQ-05 (Nueces River at Calallen - upstream gauge)
How did a hurricane turn into five weeks without safe tap water?
nodes.conclusion: Natural cascade: surge and wind take both power feeds to the water plant, pumps fail, pressure drops citywide, a boil-water notice follows and stomach illness rises; replacement pump parts are delayed because the supplier's warehouse flooded and the port is closed. No adversary.
key_joins: weather and gauges -> scada_historian by time
scada_historian tag -> work_orders asset_id
work_orders vendor_id -> cargo_manifests supplier_id -> port_arrivals mmsi
eas_alerts area_id -> ed_visits/syndromic by area and day

nodes.label: Whose fuel fouled the air station's generator?
nodes.conclusion: A tanker goes dark at the offshore anchorage while another boat's identity appears beside it; fuel moves to a barge and is delivered under the emergency fuel contract; the generator later fails on that lot.
key_joins: ais mmsi gap + port_surveillance radar contact with no AIS at the same place and time
ais identity seen in two places (shore feed vs satellite feed)
fuel_deliveries lot_id/contract_id -> contracts supplier_id -> base_status_reports equipment_id

nodes.label: Are the debris contractor and the fuel supplier connected?
nodes.conclusion: Two emergency contractors share a registered address, a bank account and (later, in filings) an owner; one bills 2.3 times the surveyed debris tonnage; both receive diverted aid payments.
key_joins: contracts_vendor_registry bank_account_id shared by two supplier_id
contracts_invoices quantity vs contracts_debris_monitoring estimated tons by area and period
financial_transactions counterparty/account -> the same accounts

nodes.label: Who took over 410 aid accounts, and was it planned?
nodes.conclusion: One network probes the aid portal weeks before the storm, sends the phishing wave after landfall, then runs automated sign-in attempts and changes deposit details on 410 accounts; the rumor accounts link to the same lookalike site.
key_joins: portal_access_logs client network in August, September and November
portal_access_logs account_ref = aid_applications account_id (deposit changes) -> financial_transactions account_id
social_media url host = mail gateway sender domain in host_audit_logs

nodes.label: Did every neighborhood get the same help?
nodes.conclusion: Low-income surge-zone tracts wait about twice as long for a unit and receive about half their share of aid dollars; the cause is access and distance, not an adversary.
key_joins: cad_911 census_tract -> census income quartile; response time = first_arrival - call_received
aid_applications tract dollars vs census population
avl unit travel vs bridge and road closures

nodes.label: Why did two moored tankers spill 9,000 barrels as the storm arrived?
nodes.conclusion: A vendor's remote-maintenance account connects to both ships' cargo-control systems from an unfamiliar network and opens cargo valves from 04:00Z to 05:30Z on landfall night while alarms are silenced; the crews close them by hand.
key_joins: vessel_ot_logs remote session_id -> valve command records on both mmsi
vessel_ot_logs time -> water_quality nearest sonde within the hour
port_surveillance cameras/berth_id and ais mmsi: the ships never move

nodes.label: Was the channel blast an accident?
nodes.conclusion: Drone overflights of the air station while its sensors are down, a vessel loitering dark off the entrance channel two weeks before the blast, GPS interference traced to a parked transmitter during the relief airlift, and then a device beside a tug: one actor using the storm to hold the port shut.
key_joins: drone_detections sensor status + sighting reports on the same nights
ais gap + port_surveillance radar track near the entrance channel -> position of the blast (ais tug mmsi, cad_911 incident)
adsb nic/nac_p degradation by time and distance from one point

nodes.label: Does the aerial imagery agree with the utility's account of the outages?
nodes.conclusion: Survey passes over the substations show open breakers in yards with no flood or wind damage, first at one substation and after the second command at another; thermal readings show equipment that cooled without a fault.
key_joins: drone_telemetry mission_name/tile set -> damage_assessment utility_site_survey asset_id
thermal_survey_readings asset_id -> outage_map substation_id and time
adsb icao24 of the survey aircraft -> flight log

nodes.label: What did the port's own sensors see?
nodes.conclusion: Cameras and radar give an independent record: the two tankers intact at the berth until the cameras lose power; later, radar holds a contact with no AIS where the anchored tanker reports a gap, and a small craft leaves it toward the entrance channel.
key_joins: port_surveillance camera berth_id/time vs vessel_ot_logs
port_surveillance radar track with ais_correlated = false vs ais gap for the mmsi at that position
port_conditions segment status at the time

nodes.label: What does the 911 record say about the storm, hour by hour?
nodes.conclusion: Volume peaks the day after landfall, rescue calls the day after that; a cluster of calls near utility sites with no victims comes from prepaid numbers; the boil-water day produces its own surge of non-emergency calls.
key_joins: cad_911 daily counts vs cbecc_daily_call_volume
cad_911 callback_number -> ali_subscriber_records class of service
cad_911 incident_number -> sar_missions / avl

nodes.label: How late were the Spanish-language warnings, and did it matter?
nodes.conclusion: Spanish versions of alerts trail the English by hours every time and by more than twelve hours for the Districts 3 and 4 boil-water notice; Spanish-speaking households in those districts show the earliest and largest rise in stomach illness.
key_joins: eas_alerts ReleasedAt_EN vs ReleasedAt_ES by alert_id
broadcast_logs translation_jobs alert_id -> first_aired
ed_visits Preferred_Language and Patient_Tract by day after the notice

nodes.label: Were the rumors organic?
nodes.conclusion: About forty accounts created in the same weeks post the same sentences in the same fifteen-minute slots, push the false home-seizure and refinery-negligence stories and a lookalike aid site, and go silent the day the platforms announce removals; a second set wakes up later.
key_joins: social_media text reuse + created_at slots by screen_name
social_media url host -> the lure domain in mail logs
_platform_records_return account status dates

nodes.label: What pushed the hospitals past capacity twice?
nodes.conclusion: First the storm (trauma, generator power, a fuel scare), then a stomach-illness wave from the water system that is larger at the hospital serving Districts 3 and 4 and among Spanish-speaking patients.
key_joins: hospital_capacity by facility_id and day
ed_visits CC_Category by tract and language
fuel_deliveries facility_id tank dips; outage_map feeder to the hospital

nodes.label: Who was rescued, where, and by whom?
nodes.conclusion: About 1,400 rescues in five days, concentrated in Flour Bluff, North Beach and Calallen; helicopters hoist where boats cannot reach; some welfare checks near utility sites find no one.
key_joins: sar_missions asset_id -> adsb icao24 / avl unit_id
sar_missions incident_number -> cad_911
flood_depth_soundings by tract

nodes.label: Who was flying drones over the substation and the docks before the storm?
nodes.conclusion: Detections with no authorization on five evenings before landfall over one substation and the tanker berth, and on six nights after landfall over the air station while its sensors were degraded; bearings from two sensors cross at a marina berth.
key_joins: drone_detections authorization_id empty vs laanc_authorizations
bearing lines from two sensor_id at the same time -> a position
that position -> terminal_registry slip -> ais mmsi berthed there

nodes.label: Where did the oil go, and who breathed it?
nodes.conclusion: Hydrocarbons rise first at the sonde beside the berth within the hour of the valve opening, then at the bay sondes over two days; downwind air monitors and nearby emergency rooms show the same footprint.
key_joins: vessel_ot_logs valve time -> water_quality sensor_id order of arrival
air_quality sensor_id by wind direction (weather)
syndromic area_id respiratory and skin complaints

nodes.label: Did every alert reach every station?
nodes.conclusion: Each official alert can be followed from issue to relay to air; one relay station lags every time, most stations are off the air through landfall, and the Spanish station learns of the Districts 3 and 4 notice the next morning.
key_joins: eas_alerts alert_id -> broadcast alert_relay_log -> station_program_log
station_status_log off-air windows

nodes.label: Which storm claims were never real?
nodes.conclusion: One property company holds policies whose replacement values were raised months before the storm through the same broker and appraisers, files 187 near-identical claims within days through a small set of adjusters, and a storm-chasing contractor's invoices support them.
key_joins: insurance_claims policy_transaction (pre-storm value increases) -> claim by holder_id/policy_id
claims text reuse and adjuster_id concentration
aid_applications and contracts supplier_id for the contractor

nodes.label: Why did parts of the city lose power again after the storm?
nodes.conclusion: Someone using an engineer's credentials from outside Texas changed a relay threshold and a relay file during the storm-preparation freeze and later opened two breakers; the outages look like storm damage but the commands have no operator and no work order.
key_joins: host_audit_logs remote_access_sessions time window -> ot_config_changes / scada_command_log in the same window
scada_historian setting tag change time = config change time (to the second)
outage_map substation_id re-outage time = command time; work_orders: no matching order
damage_assessment utility survey: breaker open with no storm damage

nodes.label: Why did Districts 3 and 4 lose water pressure two weeks after the storm?
nodes.conclusion: A pump setpoint and a booster setpoint are lowered in one late-night remote session and the low-pressure alarms are suppressed; pressure in the zone falls slowly until a field operator notices and the boil-water notice is issued; illness follows, worst where the Spanish notice arrived late.
key_joins: scada_historian setpoint tags step at 02:04Z/02:08Z = ot_config_changes rows = remote session window
alarm_suppression_audit adds -> no low-pressure alarm in historian
eas_alerts English vs Spanish release -> ed_visits by language and tract

nodes.label: How did the intrusion stay hidden for six weeks?
nodes.conclusion: Every action is timed to look like storm effects: changes during the freeze, commands during restoration switching, alerts auto-acknowledged by an exception rule created weeks earlier, analysts in storm mode bulk-dismissing the rest.
key_joins: siem rule_changes (exception rule, storm mode) -> dispositions of the alerts that mattered
siem_alerts time = remote session time = historian change time
zeek periodic outbound connection first/last seen vs isolation day

nodes.label: What did the security operations centre see, and when could it have known?
nodes.conclusion: The first outbound connection is alerted and closed as a false positive; the historian sessions are auto-acknowledged by an exception rule nobody approved; storm mode dismisses three alerts that mattered; the anomaly model finally flags the fourteenth session.
key_joins: siem_alerts alert family by time -> disposition and closer
rule_changes created_by and ticket -> historian_access account
zeek conn/ssl for the alerted destination
